"She probably heard about how delicious his food is," Ally said loyally.
"Yeah, that makes sense," Barry said. "I'm sure you're right."

He gushed for a few minutes about Ray's cooking, but Ally couldn't tell if Barry actually meant what he was saying. Something about Barry was beginning to strike her as odd. Still, she'd been on Earth for only a little while. There was a lot she still didn't understand about human behavior.

Barry ate another bite of his sandwich and then looked at his watch. "I've got to get home. My . . . father is expecting me," he added quickly. "See you tomorrow." And with that, he raced out of the diner.
Randy scratched his head. "He's an odd one."
Ally nodded. "I hope we didn't make a mistake by hiring him."
Ray shrugged. "You were odd at first too, Ally," he said, laughing.
"I was, wasn't I?" Ally grinned. "And look how great I worked out!"
Later Ally returned to her pod in the park. She took off her meld medallion and reverted to her Astralian form.
"Ahh." She stretched. "That feels so much better."
As Ally sat down at the control panel, the computer whirled to life. "Scanning the area. And detecting no new parts or fuel cells in the immediate vicinity."
Ally sighed. "Bad news, Alpha. I couldn't find them. I'll have to search again tomorrow."
"Searching is unnecessary," the computer said. "I have computed the exact location of the fuel cells and parts required to repair this pod."
"What?" Ally cried. "That's fabulous news! Where are they?"
The computer spat out a printout.
Ally grabbed it. But her face quickly fell.
"The parts are in the Sandville UFO Museum?" She groaned. "That can't be right, Alpha. I went there this morning. They don't sell anything we need in the gift shop."
"The items are not in the gift shop," the computer said. "They are located in the museum's northeast quadrant."
"Huh?"
The computer printed out another document. This one showed a map of the museum.
Ally studied it closely and then let out an even louder groan. "I know this location—it's Dr. Lloyd's office!"
She jumped to her feet and started pacing around the pod. She thought as hard as she could. But there was only one option: she'd have to go to Dr. Lloyd's opening on Friday.
"Wake up!" the computer said. "This is your second wake-up call!"
Ally sat up in bed and yawned. "It's morning already? But I just went to sleep."
"You went dormant at one o'clock in the morning. You had five hours of sleep, three hours less than your standard resting period."
"I was too worried to sleep. I have to figure out a way to sneak into Dr. Lloyd's office at the exhibit opening. And I have no good ideas."
The computer whirred. "According to my analysis, the gallery has perfect acoustics when it's empty. Advice: create a diversion to distract Dr. Lloyd."
"What do perfect acoustics have to do with anything?" Ally asked.
"You can activate your voice-throwing ability to call Dr. Lloyd away to another part of the museum."
"Brilliant! Why didn't I think of that?"
Alpha's lights blinked. "You do not possess my superior computing powers."
"True." Ally jumped up and did a quick dance move. "And you do not possess my superior dance powers!"
"Morning, Ally!" Mateo said when Ally got to work. He was sitting at the counter with Phil.
"Hi, Mateo," Ally said. "Phil, you're here early today."
"The next few days are going to be very busy at the museum with the sci-fi convention," Phil replied. "So I'm going golfing today."
"Where's golfing?" Ally asked.
Mateo laughed. "Are you still half asleep, Ally? Phil is going to play golf."
"Oh, right!" Ally faked a laugh. "Silly me!"
"Golfing is relaxing and makes me happy," Phil said.
"Hmm," Ally thought. Would golfing make Ray happier too?
Ally found Ray in his office. "Did you know Phil is going golfing today?"
"Yep."
"Why don't you go with him," she suggested.
"I can't leave the diner."
"Sure you can. Randy can cook. You haven't taken any time off since we reopened."
Ray gazed at her. "Maybe I could take a few hours."
Ally nodded. "Go have fun. It'll make you happy!"
After the men left, Mateo called Ally over.
"Thank you for encouraging Papi to take time off. Ever since my mom left, he's had trouble relaxing. He worries about the diner and me too much."
"So that's why Ray is lonely!" Ally thought. "His wife left."
"Is that your mom in the photo on his desk?" she asked.
Mateo nodded.
"Has Ray ever tried to meet someone new?"
Mateo shrugged. "He says he's too old to date."
"Who's too old to date?" Kate asked, entering the diner.
After Ally explained, Kate shook her head.
"You're never too old to find love," she said. "That's what my aunt says. She's single, and she's about Ray's age."
"Maybe they could date each other!" Ally thought.
"I've got to get to soccer camp," Mateo said. "See you tomorrow for the convention."
Ally waited for Mateo to leave before whispering her great idea to Kate.
"Yes, let's do it!" Kate squealed. "I'll tell my aunt and you tell Ray. We can arrange to have them meet here tomorrow before we go to the convention."
"Awesome!" Ally was excited that she'd found another way to make Ray happy.
"Do you still want to go shopping today after your shift?" Kate asked.
"Yes! Shopping and matchmaking sounds like the perfect day to me!"
Later that afternoon, as Ally and Kate walked downtown, Ally noticed something very strange: there were alien creatures everywhere!
She glanced at Kate, but the other girl didn't seem to notice a thing.
"Maybe my imagination is playing tricks on me," Ally thought. She blinked a few times, but the aliens were still there.
"Um, Kate, why are there so many aliens around?"
Kate laughed. "I wish Sandville was known for something more interesting than the UFO museum. But I do like the sci-fi convention. It's fun, and everybody dresses up in crazy costumes."
"Oh!" Ally laughed. "They're costumes!"
Kate gave her an odd look. "What did you think they were? Which reminds me, we need costumes too."
"Why?" Ally asked.
"If we don't wear them to the convention, we'll never hear the end of it from Mateo and Bethany. Let's go into that store across the street," Kate suggested. "They have fun stuff."
Ally started to follow Kate across the street. But just then she spotted a huge billboard: "The Sandville Sci-Fi Convention Presents Dr. Cosmo Lloyd and a Special Out-of-This-World Guest!"
Beside the words, for the entire town to see, was a silhouette of . . . an Astralian!
Ally gasped. "Is that me?"

Ally tossed and turned all night long, convinced that Dr. Lloyd knew her secret. Even worse, he was going to reveal it to the whole world tomorrow at the sci-fi convention. Everyone would soon know that she was an alien from Astralia.
"There is a 5 percent possibility that the billboard is not referring to you," the computer announced the next morning.
"But Dr. Lloyd invited me to be his special guest!" Ally said. "Of course the billboard refers to me."
"In that case, it would be illogical for you to go to the museum today."
"But if I don't go, I'll never get the stuff we need!" Ally wailed.
"In that case, it would be illogical for you not to go," Alpha said.
"Ugh!" Ally said. "You're right. I have no choice." She put on her meld medallion and changed to her human form.
"Here I go," she said as she headed for the door. "I'll see you later."
The computer blinked but stayed silent. For once Alpha didn't seem to have anything to say.

Ally was meeting the others at the diner. When she arrived, Flo was waiting on tables, and Ray was cooking in the kitchen. The tables were filled with customers. Almost everyone was wearing an alien costume.
"Wow, you guys look terrific!" Ally said as Mateo and Bethany entered, wearing costumes too—the red uniforms of crew members from Cosmic Quest , a popular TV show.
"Thanks!" Bethany said. "Is Kate here yet? She said she has a big surprise for us."
"A surprise?" Ally gasped. "I forgot to tell Ray about the date that Kate and I arranged!"
She turned to run into Ray's office, but it was too late. Kate and a woman wearing a fancy dress and high heels were walking into the diner.
"Hello," the woman said. "I'm Kate's aunt Destiny. I'm here to see Ray."
Mateo grinned. "Papi, you have a visitor!"
Ray came into the dining room. "Can I help you?" he asked, wiping his hands on his apron, which was splattered with food stains.
Aunt Destiny took one look at Ray and scowled. "I came all the way across town to meet him," she whispered loudly to Kate. "But he didn't even bother to wash up! Sorry, Kate, but I'm leaving!"
Aunt Destiny marched out of the diner.
Ray shook his head. "I have no idea what just happened, but I'm too busy for this crazy stuff," he said, heading back to the kitchen.
Mateo looked from Ally to Kate. "What was that all about?"
"That was all about making a mess of things," Kate mumbled.
"It's my fault," Ally moaned. "I forgot to tell Ray that Kate and I invited her aunt here to meet him!"
Flo overheard them. "Don't worry about it, girls. I'll cheer him up later with a few jokes I heard on TV last night."
"Thanks for trying," Mateo said to Ally. "And Papi did enjoy playing golf yesterday."
"That's good." Ally sighed.
"Uh-oh! Look at the time!" Bethany said. "We have to get to the convention. Where's your costume, Ally?"
"I have our costumes!" Kate pulled two pairs of pointy ears and antennae out of a bag. "We got them yesterday. And if anyone asks what we are, we're going to say we're cute aliens!"
When Ally and her friends arrived at the museum, Phil quickly spotted them and waved them over. He let them in through a side door.
"That was so nice of Phil," Mateo said. "He saved us a lot of time waiting in line. So where should we go first?"
"I want to ride the space rocket simulator. I hear it makes you feel like you're flying in space," Bethany said.
"Me too," Mateo and Kate agreed.

Ally had no idea what they were talking about. But she had other things to do. "I, uh, don't like rides. I'll meet up with you guys later. Have fun!" She hurried off before they could say anything more.
"That was easy!" Ally thought. "I hope getting my parts is just as easy."
But when Ally arrived at Dr. Lloyd's exhibit hall, she realized that this task would be anything but easy.
A guard stood at the metal detector at the entrance to the hall.
"I can't go through that metal detector!" Ally thought. "The guard will make me take off my meld medallion. Ugh! What am I going to do now?"
The security guard stared at Ally. "You just going to stand there, or are you coming in?" she asked gruffly.
"Uh . . ." Ally hesitated. "Not yet. Thanks!"

Ally spun around and skittered away. "I have to find a quiet place to think," she thought. She found a restroom around the corner and ducked inside. She was hoping it would be empty, but several humans were inside, adjusting their costumes.
Ally looked closely at their costumes and makeup. One girl was dressed like a rocket ship, and the other one wore a pair of enormous ears.
"Yikes," Ally thought. "Earthlings know nothing about the universe. Nobody has ears like that!"
Ally looked at another costume. Suddenly she knew what she had to do.
"It's risky," she thought, swallowing hard. "But it's my only choice."

She stepped into one of the stalls and took off her meld medallion, instantly reverting to her Astralian form. As she stepped back out of the stall, she froze, waiting for someone to react to her appearance. But to her relief, no one even looked at her.
Ally grinned and headed for the hallway. "It worked!" she thought. "Now I just need a hiding spot for my meld medallion so I can pass through the metal detector."
She looked around and spotted a fire extinguisher. "No one will bother to look here," she thought, tucking the meld medallion behind it. "As long as there's no fire, that is."
Ally started back to the gallery. On the way people kept stopping her.
"Cool costume!" a tall alien said.
"Yeah," a purple one agreed. "With that outfit, you could win the contest!"
Ally nodded and gave a thumbs-up sign. But if everything went smoothly, she would be heading back to her pod with the parts in a few minutes.
Ally marched past the guard, through the metal detector, and right into Dr. Lloyd's gallery. "I'm almost there!" she thought excitedly.
But her excitement drained away a second later.
"There are too many people here!" Ally thought. "There's no way I can sneak into his office without being seen. And the room is too crowded for me to use my voice-throwing ability."
Just then Dr. Lloyd stepped up to a podium. To his right was a large box covered by a curtain. The lights dimmed and he began to speak.

"Thank you for coming, sci-fi fans and extraterrestrial experts!" he said. "As many of you surely know, I've spent my entire career searching for alien life. While I believe there are several advanced civilizations in the universe, there is only one species who travels the universe, trying to establish peace and solve intergalactic disputes."
Ally's stomach clenched. "Uh-oh," she thought. "Here it comes. He's going to reveal my secret to everyone."
"I've devoted most of my studies to these beings," Dr. Lloyd continued. "And now, through extensive research, I can finally present to you . . . an up-close specimen!"

Ally covered her face, certain that he was about to call her up onstage. But Dr. Lloyd didn't even look at her. Instead he pulled a cord on the curtain covering the box. It fell away to reveal . . . a figure made of wax!
Ally slowly peeked out from behind her fingers. "The nose is wrong," she thought, "and its feet are way too small. But it does look a lot like an Astralian!"

A good Astralian would speak up right now, Ally thought. An Astralian would never allow a human to spread false knowledge about the species. But as the humans began to move closer to view the wax figure, Ally was thinking of something else: this was her chance to slip into Dr. Lloyd's office.
A moment later she was inside. She quietly closed the door behind her and pulled out the map printout.

"According to this map, the parts should be in that cabinet," she murmured. She ran over and flung open the door. But to her horror, the cabinet was almost empty. The only thing inside was a small black box with an antenna and a red blinking light.
"Not again!" Ally moaned. "This time Alpha got the location wrong!"
She looked around and started frantically rummaging through other cabinets, hoping that she'd find the parts. Then— bam! She gasped as the door to the office flew open.
A tall, thin woman with glasses and a scowl on her face was standing in the doorway of the office. "What are you doing in here?"
"Uh . . . I was just . . . ," Ally stammered.
"This isn't a changing room!" the woman snapped, stepping into the room. "This is Dr. Lloyd's private office. You should have found somewhere else to get ready for the costume contest."
Ally almost laughed. "She thinks this is a costume!" she thought.
"So sorry!" Ally scurried for the door.
"You'd better hurry." The woman's voice softened slightly. "I think the costume contest began a few minutes ago."
"Oh, I'm not entering the contest," Ally said.
"Why not? There's a hundred-dollar prize, and you've got the best costume here."

Before Ally could say anything else, the woman led her out of the office and took her to the main exhibit hall. Sure enough, a group of humans in costumes stood onstage while two judges walked around, inspecting them.
"If we put an asteroid sticker on your back, that means you advance to the next round!" a judge called out.
"Get on up there!" Dr. Lloyd's assistant gently pushed Ally up.
Ally scooted to the back, behind the other contestants. She started to sneak off the stage, but one of the judges had spotted her.
"Your costume definitely earns you a spot in the next round!" The judge slapped an asteroid sticker on her.
Ally gulped. "Now I'll never be able to sneak away," she thought.

Soon the contest was down to Ally and a kid dressed as Martian Man. Ally shook her head. She'd been to Mars once on a peace mission with her parents. And this kid didn't look anything like a real Martian.
"I don't want to be mean," Ally thought. "But my costume is so much more authentic." She did a quick dance move to entertain the audience, and several humans clapped and cheered.

Ally grinned. She hadn't wanted to enter the contest, and she definitely needed to go look for those parts. But a part of her was having fun. "This contest is like a fashion show," she thought. "And I'm definitely going to win that cash prize!"
Everyone was eagerly waiting for the winner to be announced. As the judges huddled together, talking, Ally looked out at the spectators again.
"Oh no!" she thought, spotting her friends. She covered her face. "What if they recognize me?"
But the only one looking at her was Mateo. And he didn't even blink.
At last a judge stepped forward. "We saw a lot of wonderful costumes today, but there's one that truly stands out. The winner of the Sandville UFO Convention costume contest is . . ."
A drumroll sounded over the speakers. Ally stood up taller and fluffed her tentacles. She wanted to look good and take an Astralian bow when she accepted the prize.
The drumroll ended and the judge said, "Martian Man!"
"What?" Ally felt like she'd been punched. Several seconds passed before she understood what had just happened. She'd lost the alien costume contest!
"Ridiculous!" she thought, stomping offstage. "Humans are so ignorant about other beings in the universe!" Ally felt angry, but she had a bigger problem—she had to get back into Dr. Lloyd's office.

In the gallery Dr. Lloyd was still talking. "I've finally achieved a breakthrough in my efforts to communicate with extraterrestrials." He placed a small black box with a blinking light on the podium. It was the one Ally had seen in the cabinet.
"My beacons have been sending signals out into space. They are specially designed to attract aliens to Earth. And I have proof that my experiment finally worked."
"What?" Ally stared at the screen in horror as Dr. Lloyd played a video. It showed her escape pod approaching Earth.
"I believe this spaceship landed somewhere in Sandville, and it's still here," Dr. Lloyd announced. "And I intend to find it!"
Everyone gasped, including Ally.
"How do the beacons work?" someone asked.

"Through advanced technology, the beacons send a signal to communicate to the spaceship that there's something here it needs," Dr. Lloyd explained. "It could be food, fuel, or even spare parts. But of course, that's just a trick to lure the ship here."
"A trick?" Ally stood, stunned. "I was tricked into landing on Earth?" she thought. Did that mean she wouldn't find any parts or fuel here?
Tears slipped down her cheeks as she ran out of the gallery and retrieved her meld medallion.
She slipped it over her head and was about to leave the museum when she heard a gasp behind her.
"Ally?"
Ally froze with fear. She had two choices: she could pretend she didn't hear whoever was behind her and walk away. Or, choice two, she could run away!
But before she could do anything at all, the person stepped in front of her.
Mateo's eyes were wide, and his jaw hung open. "Did what I think just happened really just happen? That was . . . Are you a . . . ?"
"Please, Mateo, don't tell anyone what you saw," Ally pleaded. "My ship broke down. I need parts and fuel, and once I get them, I'm going to leave. I came to Earth in peace!"
"I knew it," he murmured. "When I saw you onstage before . . ."
"Please don't tell anyone!" Ally repeated. "It could put me in danger!"
"I won't," Mateo said. "But I do have to say one thing."
Ally gulped.
"You were robbed!" he said.
"Someone stole my pod?"
"No." Mateo smiled. "You totally should have won first prize in the contest!"
Ally laughed with relief. "Oh! I agree. So you're not mad at me for lying to you?"
"No way," Mateo said. "I mean, how many people can say their good friend is an alien?"
Touched, Ally put a hand on her heart. "You think of me as your good friend?"
"We haven't known each other long, but you've been really helpful to Papi and me."
Ally's eyes filled with tears. An Earthling was calling her a good friend! Her parents would be thrilled at all the peaceful cooperation she'd achieved on this planet.
"I'll make you a deal," Mateo said. "Since I know your big secret, I'll tell you mine."
"You don't have to do that," Ally said.

"I want to," Mateo replied. "I've never told this to anyone. I know where my mom is. She texts me. She's trying to pursue a new career and live on her own. But she's worried if my dad knows, he'll try to convince her to come back home."
"Wow, that's a huge secret," Ally said. "Thank you for trusting me with it."
"Well, it's not quite as big as being an alien," Mateo said. "So where are these parts you need?"
Ally got teary-eyed again. "I thought they were here in Sandville, but it turns out Dr. Lloyd lured my ship here. So . . ." She swallowed hard. "I don't know if I'll ever get home."
Mateo put an arm around her shoulder. "I'll help you figure it out. For now, why don't we find the others and head back to the diner."
As Ally and Mateo headed to the main hall, she told him all about Dr. Lloyd's discoveries.
"His research has lots of inaccuracies," she said. "But he's not totally misinformed. And if he finds out about me, I bet he'll . . ." She swallowed hard again. "Try to use me for more research!"
At the diner Barry was wiping down tables, and Flo and Ray were chatting behind the counter.
"Hey, kids!" Ray greeted them with a big smile. "How was the convention?"
"Interesting." Mateo traded glances with Ally.
"How about some ice cream on the house?" Ray said.
"Yes!" everyone said.
"He's in a good mood," Mateo whispered to Ally.
Ally nodded. Ray did seem happy, and she knew why: Ray's and Flo's thoughts were suddenly coming to her loud and clear. They were both thinking about how much they enjoyed each other's company.
"I did make Ray happy," Ally thought. "I did it by hiring Flo!" It was another good deed that would impress her parents.
Ally was about to dig into her bowl of ice cream when Barry came over. "When are you going to teach me that levitating trick?"
"Why is he so desperate to learn that?" Ally thought, annoyed. She did a quick scan of his thoughts, but all she could see was an image of a man, likely his father, looking proud.
She felt her heart soften. "I understand that feeling," she thought. "I want my parents to be proud of me too."
"Soon, Barry." Ally held crossed fingers behind her back, the way humans did when telling white lies.
For once Barry took that for an answer and walked away.
Ally kept her fingers crossed for another minute. But it wasn't because she was about to tell another lie. It was because humans often crossed their fingers for another reason—luck.
With Mateo's help, maybe she could figure out a way to get home soon.
"Who's ready to greet the guest of honor?" the bandleader asked the party crowd. Everyone went wild, cheering. "Here she is at long last, Allyzooba Delta5X of Astralia!"
Ally glided onto the dance floor. She twirled, showing off her new dress. "I'm so happy to finally be back home on—"
"That does not compute," Alpha interrupted.
Ally opened her eyes and groaned. She wasn't back on Astralia. She was in her bed in her pod, still on Earth.
"It's time for your morning dance party," Alpha said as music blared from her speakers.
"Not today, Alpha." Ally got out of bed. "My dream made me sad. I thought I'd be home by now."
"Disappointment is a logical response," Alpha said. "Advice: consider the positives."

Ally sighed. "I'll try to stay positive. I have a good friend in Mateo, who'll keep my identity a secret. He also offered to help me get parts so I can fix the pod. Oh, I forgot to tell you—he's stopping by this morning."
"Warning!" Alpha blared. "Astralian camouflage will not work with an alien on board."
"Calm down. He won't be here long—I have to go to work," Ally replied. "He just wants to see my pod. I'll camouflage it as soon as we leave."
Mateo arrived a short while later. His eyes went wide as he looked around. "This pod is awesome. I wish we could go flying!"
"Proposal," Alpha said. "If the human can assist in repairing the pod, a short flight can be authorized."
"Whoa!" Mateo said. "I've got a smartphone, but it's not as smart as your computer!"
"Alpha knows everything there is to know in the entire universe," Ally said. "You can ask her anything."
"Anything?" Mateo said. "Hmm. Bethany and I have been dating for one month. Got any super fun ideas for an anniversary surprise?"
"Allyzooba is a superior resource for that question," Alpha replied. "Astralians must use their Astral minds to help others in the universe."
"I'll come up with a fun idea," Ally said. "But for now we should focus on the pod parts. Alpha, can you print out the list again?"
When it was ready, Mateo looked it over. "I'm not sure how to get rocket fuel, but I think we can make beta-booster coils from old mattress springs. And I know exactly where to get some."
"Great!" Ally said. "Let's get going."
Ally grabbed her meld medallion and hurried to the door.
"Warning," Alpha called. "Do not forget to camouflage the pod."
"I know." Ally rolled her eyes. "Let's go, Mateo."
"Wait!" Mateo said. "You still look like an Astralian."
"Oops!" As Ally led the way out of the pod, she slipped her meld medallion over her neck. She immediately changed into human form.
"Watching you transform like that is amazing!" Mateo said.
"You mean like this?" Ally said. Mateo laughed as Ally toggled between her Astralian and human forms until she got dizzy. "Phew! That's enough of that!"

Ally and Mateo headed downtown. Along the way they noticed some new sculptures installed in different spots. There was a giant red heart with the words Love Your Mother (Earth); an oversize sunflower; and three sheep grazing on grass in a traffic median.
"What are these sculptures?" Ally asked.
"Sandville hired an artist to create public art with an ecological theme," Mateo said. "And the coolest thing is, she's reusing stuff she finds around town."
"Everything gets reused on Astralia," Ally said. "I'm glad to see humans thinking about wasting less on Earth."
"Speaking of not wasting stuff . . ." Mateo held up his phone. "The Sandville Mattress Factory offers old springs for free."
"Springs?" Ally said, confused.
"They're coils," Mateo said.
"Oh! Do we have time to check it out before I go to work?"
"I think so." Mateo spoke to his phone: "Mira, where is Sandville Mattress Factory?"
"1515 West 19th Street," Mateo's phone replied.
"You have an Alpha too!" Ally said.
Mateo laughed. "Yep. But like I said, Mira isn't nearly as smart as Alpha!"
A short while later, Ally and Mateo arrived at the diner with a bag of springs. Ray was sitting in a booth, surrounded by cookbooks.
"What's all this, Papi?" Mateo asked.
"I've got a problem," Ray said. "The League of Rocket Scientists wants to hold its annual gala here."
"Why is that a problem?" Mateo asked.
Ray dropped his head into his hands. "Because it's next week!"
"Wow," Ally thought. "Ray is nervous about this gala."

"The League of Rocket Scientists read about the diner in Gourmet Greta's column," Ray said. "They love our space theme, but they want a special menu for their dinner. I was thinking of serving grilled salmon, but what would I call it?"
"I bet Ally can think of some out-of-this-world ideas," Mateo said.
"Solar Salmon!" Ally suggested.
"Hey, Ray," Randy, the assistant cook, called from Ray's office. "You've got a phone call."
"Coming!" Ray hurried to his office.
"Ally, what are some of the best meals in the galaxy?" Mateo asked.

"Hmm . . . I'd say Formarian Frittata and . . ." Ally trailed off when she spotted the new waiter, Barry, outside, taking pictures of the diner. Ally had learned a lot about humans, but Barry's behavior was still mysterious to her at times. "What's he taking pictures of?"
Mateo turned to look, but as soon as Barry saw them looking, he put his phone away. Then he rushed inside and sat down at the counter next to Phil.
Mateo shrugged. "Why does Barry do a lot of the things he does?"
Ally quickly read Barry's mind, but as usual, he was thinking about ways to make his father proud.
"Back to ideas for Ray," Ally said. "Formarian Frittata would make a great appetizer. And Meltron Moon Pies could be a fun dessert, oh, and—"
"That was the league's secretary on the phone." Ray hurried over. "They want to make sure that you work at the gala, Ally. They want to see your tricks."
"Sure!" Ally said brightly. But inside she was nervous. "Do these rocket scientists want to be entertained?" she thought. "Or have they heard rumors about me? I'd better be careful."
"Tricks? Gala?" Barry's ears perked up. "Can I work too, Ray? Please?"
Ray nodded. "I need everyone that night." He gathered up the cookbooks and went to the kitchen.
Barry looked at Ally. "Now you'll have to teach me your tricks."
Ally sighed. "Fine. We can begin tomorrow when we're both working."
"Yes!" Barry pumped his arm in triumph and went back to sit with Phil.
Mateo shot her a look. "You can't teach him how to levitate a plate, can you?" he whispered.

"Of course not," Ally said. "But he keeps asking me to teach him tricks, and I can't keep making excuses. That might make him even more suspicious of me. Don't worry." She glanced at the bag of coils. "I have a plan."
Mateo nodded, but he still looked worried. "I hope it works. I'm meeting Bethany for a bike ride in the park. See you later."
After Ally started her shift, one of her first customers was a woman at the counter. She barely looked up from her phone when Ally came to take her order.
"I'll have five gallons of silver paint, please," the woman said.
"We only serve yellow paint here," Ally joked.
The woman looked up and laughed. "Sorry! I'm so distracted by my work."
"Why do you need silver paint?" Ally asked.
"I've been commissioned by the Sandville Arts Board to create sculptures from objects found or seen around town. I need silver paint to finish a sculpture."
"I've seen a few of your sculptures—they're great!" Ally said.
"Thanks," the artist replied. "I still have one more piece to make. I'm looking for something with a real wow factor."
"There are some interesting things in the park," Ally said. "The bandshell, the murals, even the trees are inspiring!"
The artist smiled. "Thanks. I'm Sarah by the way. Oh, and I'll have the Space Cakes, please."
"One order of pancakes coming up!"
As Ally went to put in Sarah's order, she had another inspiration. "I know what Mateo should do for Bethany's surprise! I can't wait to tell him!"
Ally headed home from her shift in a good mood. Even though last night's dream had made her miss home, she had a lot to be thankful for here on Earth.
"Today I helped both Ray and Sarah solve problems. By the time I get back to Astralia, I'm going to have a long list of good deeds," Ally thought. "I'll ask Alpha to keep a log for me!"
Ally stopped near the trees and held up her meld medallion to reveal her pod. But to her surprise, nothing happened. She held it up again, but still the pod didn't appear.
"Oh no!" Ally gasped. Her pod had vanished!
Ally stared at the spot in the trees where her pod should be. "It can't be gone!" she thought. "It has to be here somewhere."
"Alpha!" Ally cried. "Where are you?"
There was no answer.
Ally spent the next thirty minutes looking high and low for the pod. She'd been trying not to think the worst, but she couldn't hold the thought off any longer.
"Dr. Lloyd's machine finally worked," she thought. "He found my pod. And if he can find my pod, it won't be long before he finds me!"
Ally was close to tears as she sat down on a park bench. With her pod gone, there was no hope she'd ever get back home. But even worse, she'd lost a friend—Alpha.
Ally replayed their last morning together in her mind. That's when she realized what had happened: she’d forgotten to camouflage the pod!
"Oh no!" she moaned, burying her head in her hands. "My parents were right about me. I am totally irresponsible!"
"Ally?" Mateo rode up on his bicycle. "What's wrong?"
"It's all my fault, Mateo!" Ally moaned.
"What's your fault?" Ally heard a girl say. It was Bethany's voice, but Ally didn't see her. Mateo held up his phone—Bethany was on speakerphone.
Ally shook her head, to show Mateo she couldn't talk about it with Bethany.
"Not fault ," Mateo said quickly. "Ally told me to halt . She was joking. I'll, uh, call you later."
"Oh, okay. I—," Bethany began as Mateo hung up.
"What happened, Ally?" he asked. "You look like you’ve lost your best friend."
"I did." Ally sighed. "Alpha warned me not to forget to camouflage the pod when we left, but I was so busy trying to make you laugh, I totally forgot!"
"I don't understand. What happened to Alpha?"

"It's not just Alpha!" Ally said. "It's the entire pod. I forgot to camouflage it after we left, and Dr. Lloyd must have found it! What am I going to do? How am I going to ever get back home, and where am I going to sleep until then?"
"Whoa, whoa." Mateo gestured for Ally to slow down. "One problem at a time. Maybe someone moved the pod. Let's not jump to conclusions."
"I'm not jumping anywhere." Ally sniffled.
"I meant, we won't know what happened until we look. Come on. Let's search some more."
Ally and Mateo walked through the entire park, but the pod was nowhere to be found.
"Dr. Lloyd has it." Ally sighed. "He said he was certain he'd lured a ship to Earth. He probably took it to the UFO museum, but I can't risk going there to look for it."
"Don't worry," Mateo said. "I'll go there first thing in the morning. We'll find your pod and Alpha. I promise. And until then you'll stay with Papi and me."
"That's so nice of you." Ally blew her nose. "But what if your dad finds out I'm an Astralian?"
"You'll just have to be careful to take off your meld medallion only at night, after Papi has gone to bed."
"You don't think he'll mind having me stay?"
"Of course not." Mateo pulled out his phone. "Hi, Papi. We need a favor."
"Whatever you need, son," Ray said.
"Ally needs to stay with us for a while. You see, her place went—"
"Say no more," Ray replied. "Ally can stay in your mom's sewing room. It's not being used for anything anyway."
"Thanks, Papi!" Mateo disconnected the call. "See? We'll help you!"
Ally managed a smile. "I'm very lucky to have you and Ray for friends."
"We're lucky to have you too," Mateo said. "Let's go home. We'll find your ship and Alpha. I know we will."

As the two friends walked back to Ray's house, Ally felt a mixture of emotions. She was really sad about losing Alpha and worried she might never get back home. But she tried to think of positive things, as Alpha had advised her earlier that day.
"At least I'm learning to be a good Astralian," Ally said. "Funny how it took being light-years from home to understand what it means to be helpful."
"You're the most helpful person I know," Mateo said. "You're even willing to help weird Barry."
Ally laughed. "Hey! If I manage to teach Barry my levitation trick without making a mess of it, I might even win an Astralian Super Helper medal!"

Ally was still fast asleep when the music started playing. "Not today, Alpha," she said with a groan. But as Ally pulled up the blankets, sadness washed over her. She wasn't in the pod—she was in the sewing room at Mateo's house.
She blinked open her eyes. "Where's that music coming from?"
"From out here!" Mateo called through the closed door. "Isn't this how Alpha wakes you up every day?"
Ally didn't want to make Mateo feel bad, so she tried to wipe away her sadness. "Come on in."
"You have to work," Mateo said, "but I have the whole day to look for the pod. I'll go to the museum as soon as it opens. But first check this out."

He read from an article on his phone: 'New City-Wide Parking Ordinance. The city of Sandville has begun implementing its new zero-tolerance policy. All illegally parked vehicles will be towed to the impound lot.'
"Maybe your pod got towed," Mateo said excitedly. "Let's go to the impound lot before your shift begins."
"I'll be ready in a flash!" Ally cried.
At the impound lot, there was a long line of humans waiting to claim their cars.
"This will take all day!" Ally moaned.
"Maybe not." Mateo pointed to an area marked Oversize and Special Use Vehicles.
They walked past parked campers, school buses, and a house on wheels. But Ally's pod wasn't there.
"I really thought we would find it here," Mateo said. "I'll go to the museum now and meet you at the diner later."
"Thanks, Mateo," Ally said as they headed in different directions. "Think positive," she told herself.
"Hello there!" someone called.
Ally looked up. It was the artist, Sarah.
"Thanks for the suggestion about the park. I found some amazing objects there—and a perfect location for my new sculpture!"
Ally smiled. "I'm glad I was helpful."
"I'd love to show you the site," Sarah said. "Are you free now?"
"I have to go to work," Ally said, "but I'll stop by later."
When Ally arrived at the diner, Barry was pacing around.
"I thought you'd never get here!" he said. "I really want to learn how to levitate plates before the League of Rocket Scientists gala."
Ally took a deep breath and reminded herself to be patient. "That's not realistic, Barry," she said. "It takes a long time to learn a trick like that."
Barry frowned. "Well, I'm a super-fast learner."
"Okay." Ally shrugged. "Let's get started. The first step is learning to make it look like you're stumbling without falling."
"I've been practicing that skill. Watch this!" Barry demonstrated a perfect fake stumble.
"Whoa," Ally thought. "He has been practicing! I guess it's time for the next part of my plan. I hope it works."
Ally reached under the counter and pulled out the bag of mattress springs that she and Mateo had gotten. Next she found a package of magnets they'd used while redecorating the diner.
"I'm going to glue a magnet on one end of this spring," Ally said. "Then you'll slip your finger through the spring on the other end."
"So the magnet will stick to the plate?" Barry asked. "How?"
"Um . . ." Ally had forgotten that detail. "We put another magnet on the bottom of the plate, of course! Why don't you take care of the customers, and I'll get this trick set up."
After Ally had gotten everything together, she called Barry back over. "Practice with a paper plate. That way you can get the feel of the trick, without breaking anything."
Barry slipped the spring through his finger and then took a practice stumble. Ally was relieved when the plate stayed on the spring.
He spun toward her, his eyes narrowed. "Why don't I ever see the spring when you do it? And how do you stick magnets to customers' plates?"
Ally crossed her fingers behind her back. "I've been practicing a long time. You'll have to practice a lot. And remember, use paper plates for now!"

She hurried off to take care of customers. A minute later she saw Barry stumble, a bowl of cold cereal attached to the spring. At first it looked like the trick was going to work. But then he lost his footing and tripped for real. The bowl flew through the air—and splash! It landed in a customer's lap!
Later that day Ally was clearing off a table when she spotted Barry slipping the spring through his finger again.
"Barry!" she snapped. "I asked you not to practice at the diner anymore."
"Sorry," he said.
But as soon as Ally turned her back, Barry put a plate of eggs on the spring, tripped, and spilled eggs all over the floor.
"That's the third plate you've dropped today! Plus the bowl of cereal that landed on a customer!" Ally was trying not to get angry, but his tricks were causing problems. "Go on home. I'll clean up."
Ally had just finished cleaning up when Mateo arrived.
"Did you find my pod at the museum?" Ally asked eagerly.
"No." Mateo looked upset. "I overheard Dr. Lloyd saying that he hasn't found the ship he lured to Earth yet. But it's just a matter of time until he does!"
Ally gulped. "Dr. Lloyd will never give up looking for me!"
"At least we know he doesn't have your ship," Mateo said.
Ally drummed her fingers on the counter. "But who does?"

"Excuse me." Randy stuck his head out of the kitchen. "Is Barry gone?" When they nodded, he came out. "I saw Barry taking pictures of the food delivery today. It was weird." He scratched his head. "I'm worried that kid is up to something."
"Hmm," Mateo said. "We'll keep an eye on him."
Randy gave a thumbs-up and returned to the kitchen.
"Barry keeps causing trouble," Ally said. "Do you think he knows my secret?"
"No," Mateo said. "He's just odd."
"When I read his mind, he's always thinking about his dad. So maybe he's not suspicious of me."
Mateo changed the subject. "Ready to head home?"
"Yes," Ally said. "It's been a long day."
After Ally and Mateo left the diner, they walked by the heart sculpture.
"Oh! That reminds me," Ally said. "I promised the artist that I'd stop by the park to see her work."
"Sounds fun, let's go," Mateo said.
But entering the park reminded Ally of her lost pod again.
"I wish I knew where my pod was," she said. "And I can't believe I'm saying this, but I really miss Alpha."
"We'll find them," Mateo said. "Hey, look over there—there's a new sculpture." He pointed to a large metal ball sitting in the middle of a lawn.
Sarah waved. "I'm glad you made it. I know this doesn't look like much yet, but it's going to be a giant model of Earth, as seen from space."
Ally inspected the ball. "It would be cool if you could make it spin on its axis."
"Another great idea!" Sarah said.

Ally smiled. "My parents always told me to be helpful . . ." Ally stopped when she heard a high-pitched ping. It was faint, and she wasn't sure where it was coming from, but she'd know that sound anywhere. Ping . . . ping . . . It was an Astralian distress signal!

As soon as she could, Ally whispered to Mateo to keep Sarah busy for a few minutes. Then she followed the sound around the metal model of Earth. On one side of the sculpture, she suddenly spotted something familiar—Astralian symbols.
She stepped closer and let out a startled gasp. This model of Earth was made from cut-up pieces of metal—from her pod!
Ping . . . ping!
Even worse, that distress signal was coming from Alpha!
"I'm coming, Alpha!" Ally whispered. She crawled inside a hole in the huge hollow ball, which was filled with all kinds of junk and broken technology. "Where are you?"
Alpha's signal was fading as Ally frantically weeded through the junk. Then she spotted a motherboard with Astralian symbols. "Alpha!"
Ally crawled out of the sculpture, clutching the motherboard.

Sarah beamed when she saw Ally. "That's exactly what I want kids to do—remove junk from Earth! You see, my art is a metaphor for how we're polluting our planet, creating mounds of junk. Oh, and you found the source of that noise too. Thank goodness! It's been driving me crazy. You can keep that object, I mean, if you want it."
"I do want it," Ally said, "very badly!"
Ally and Mateo said good-bye to Sarah and rushed away.
"We have to hurry, Mateo," Ally said. "Alpha's signal is fading fast. If we don't get her connected to a power source soon, we could lose her forever!"

26.title: All Charged Up and Ready to Dance

paragraphs.text: At Ray's house Ally and Mateo were trying to bring Alpha back to life.
Ally was worried. "The signal keeps getting fainter. I've already lost my pod. I can't lose Alpha too! How are we going to charge her back up?"

Mateo tapped his chin, thinking. "There's an episode of Cosmic Quest where the crew recovers the motherboard from the crash site of their enemy's ship. They put the motherboard into a Cosmolink device to retrieve the data."
"But I don't have a Cosmolink," Ally moaned. "I don't even have a computer or phone I can put Alpha into."
Mateo grinned. Then he ran to his room and returned with a small, foldable device. "It's just a model from Cosmic Quest , but it's rechargeable. It's worth a try."
"Please work," Ally whispered as she put Alpha inside the device.
As soon as Ally closed the back, Alpha burst back to life. "I am A-A-Alpha CXB unit serial number 7638hbc81 a-a-at your service."
"Alpha!" Ally cried. "You're back. I'm sorry I lost you."
"Quick, to the ship!" Alpha said.
"What?" Ally cried.
"Roses are red, a-a-apples are green . . . 12,000 divided by 18 is equal to the trajectory of a robin in flight."
"Are you trying to be funny?" Ally asked.
"The sun is blue," Alpha replied.
Ally and Mateo exchanged worried looks.
"Let's let her charge overnight," Mateo said. "Hopefully she'll be back to herself after a full charge."
The next morning Ally was awakened by her favorite dance track. "Turn it off, Mateo. It's too loud."
But Mateo didn't reply through the door. Ally sat up and looked at the device charging nearby. Its lights were blinking, and the music was coming from its speaker.
"Alpha! You're back!"
"Affirmative," Alpha said. "Dance party time!"
Ally leaped out of bed and danced around. Soon Mateo knocked on the door and joined in the fun.
When the song ended, Alpha said, "Status report: the pod is completely destroyed."
"It's all my fault, Alpha," Ally said. "I forgot to cloak the pod when I left the park. You warned me about that—I should have listened."
"Affirmative," Alpha said. "But Alpha made a tactical error by sending out a distress signal. Instead of alerting Allyzooba, the signal attracted an intruder to the pod."
"I promise, I will keep you with me every minute of the day from now on," Ally vowed.
"And I promise to work on making the coils," Mateo said. "I think the pod is destroyed forever. But maybe we can figure out how to send a distress signal out to the galaxy to call for help."
"Alpha approves of that plan," Alpha said.
"I'd better get ready for work," Ally said. "I'm going to help Flo today with plans for the gala on Saturday."
"Speaking of which . . ." Mateo slapped his forehead. "I forgot all about my one-month anniversary with Bethany on Saturday. I still haven't thought of a fun surprise for her."

"Oh! I thought of a great idea," Ally said. "What if we plan a scavenger hunt for her? You can leave her clues and little presents all over town. My parents did that for my 85th birthday, it was so much fun!"
Mateo blinked in surprise. "You're that old?"
"I'm even older now, of course," Ally said, confused. "Why are you so surprised—do I look older than that?"
"Never mind," Mateo said. "I love your idea. I'll come by the diner later, and we can plan it all out." He left for soccer camp.
"If I can't get home to Astralia yet," Ally said to Alpha, "the next best thing is being a good Astralian and helping humans."
"Affirmative," Alpha replied.

Ally kept Alpha in her apron pocket all day at work. Luckily Barry wasn't working, so Ally didn't have to worry about him. After the breakfast rush, Ally sat down at the counter with Flo. She glanced at Ray, who was whistling as he left the kitchen and went into his office.
"Ray's mood always improves when you work, Flo," Ally said.
"I think he likes my silly jokes," Flo replied.
"Yes, that must be it." Ally smiled.
A few minutes later, Ray called Ally and Flo into the office.
"I just got a call from the league," Ray said. "Now a rocket science VIP is coming to the gala."
Ally gulped. "A VIP?" she thought. "I hope that doesn't stand for Valuable Intergalactic Predator, otherwise known as an alien hunter!"
Ally turned to Flo. "What's a VIP?" she asked nervously.
"It stands for Very Important Person," Flo said.
"Oh!" Ally sighed in relief.

"In this case, it refers to the president of the National League of Rocket Scientists," Ray said. "The local league has been trying to get him to come to their gala for years, but he always turns them down. But when he heard it was going to be here at the diner, he changed his mind."
"That's a big compliment to you, Ray," Flo said.
"You think so?" Ray asked.
Flo nodded. "Your reputation is what's bringing him here."
"But still, I think I should add some fancier dishes to the menu," Ray said.
"I'd be happy to help you come up with some ideas," Flo said.
Ray looked relieved. "Thanks, Flo. Well, I'd better get back to work."
Ally and Flo returned to the dining room.
"We should come up with an extra special dessert," Flo said. "Something to really impress the president."
Randy stepped out of the kitchen. "I can bake a special cake. I've entered a few baking contests in my day."
"You have?" Flo said. "I had no idea."

Randy pulled out his phone and showed Ally and Flo photos of some of his cakes. There was a cake that looked like a turkey dinner, one that looked like a box of cereal, and even one that looked like a cell phone.
"These are amazing!" Ally exclaimed as she scrolled through the pictures.
"I was thinking I could make a rocket ship cake for the gala," Randy said.
"That would be perfect!" Flo said.
Later Mateo came to plan the scavenger hunt with Ally.

"The one my parents planned for me was cool," Ally said. "They hid clues everywhere—all over our ship, outside, and at a playground. The final prize was a day on the moon of Formaria for me and my friends. Formaria has just enough gravity to make it like a giant bouncy house. It was so much fun."
"I wish I could take Bethany to Formaria," Mateo said.
"Me too," Ally said. "What will you make the big final prize?"

"A T-shirt from our favorite show, Cosmic Quest ," Mateo said. "I'm going to make all the gifts fit the theme of the show. And I can plant the clues here at the diner, the park, oh, and at one of the artist's sculptures. Now we just need to write some fun riddles for Bethany to solve."
"Fun riddles?" Ally said. "I already have one! What's hotter than the moon but colder than Jupiter in winter?"
Mateo shrugged. "I have no idea."
"A galactic freezer!" Ally laughed. But to her surprise Mateo just looked confused.
"Hmm," he said politely. "I'm not sure that riddle will work here on Earth. How about this one: Give me a tap and I'll give you some suds, I come in handy when you're covered in mud."
Ally scratched her head. "A solar bath?"
"No, silly." Mateo laughed. "Soap!"
"I would never have guessed that." Ally grinned. "We can leave that clue on the soap dispenser in the ladies' restroom here."
"Fantastic idea!"
That evening Ray cooked a special dinner to welcome Ally to the house.
"My famous enchiladas, just for you, Ally!" Ray said.
"These look delicious, Ray. Thank you so much for letting me stay with you," Ally said.
Ray smiled. "Like I told Mateo, I'd do anything for—"
Just then Alpha squawked loudly. "The weather on Saturn is 280 degrees with fog and rain."
Ally blushed as she pulled the device out of her pocket and sat on it. "Sorry about that! This silly device is acting up."
"No problem," Ray said. "As I was saying, I'd do—"
The device started playing loud music before quickly switching to an annoying beeping sound. While Ally was trying to get Alpha to be quiet, she saw Ray frown.
"I'm so sorry, Ray!" Ally said. "I'll go put this thing away."
She hurried upstairs. "You're still not working right, Alpha," she whispered. "I'd better put you back on the charger."
As Ally stepped back into the dining room, she heard Ray talking to Mateo.
"This house is usually so quiet, and now it's filled with noise." Ray shook his head. "What a change."
"Oh no!" Ally thought, her heart skipping a beat. "An Astralian has the duty to always be a good and peaceful guest. Alpha and I are breaking that rule!"
Ally couldn't bear the thought of upsetting Ray with Alpha's constant squawking. He had given her so much—a job, delicious meals, a place to live.
"I have to move," she told herself. "I can't stay here much longer."
She spent the whole week looking for a place that she could afford. She finally found a room to rent in a boardinghouse.
"I'll take it," Ally said to the landlord. "When can I move in?"
"Now, as long as you pay the first month's rent and—"
Ram-bam-bop-boop! Loud music interrupted the landlord.
She cupped her hands over her ears. "What's that awful noise?"
"I'm sorry. It's just my device." Ally fumbled, trying to turn the volume down on the device. "It's not working very well, and it does this sometimes."
"Well, then you can forget about renting this room!" the landlord fumed. "This is a quiet house. We don't allow loud music."
"It's not what you think," Ally said.
But the landlord led her to the front door and slammed it behind her.
Out on the street, Ally pulled Alpha out of her pocket. "This is the third time you've blurted out noise and ruined our chances of renting a room!"
"Apologies," Alpha said. "The device is scrambling Alpha's interface."
Ally sighed. "It's all my fault. If I were a responsible Astralian, I would have cloaked the pod, and none of this would ever have happened."
"Astralian wisdom says that mistakes are necessary to learning," Alpha said.

"Thanks for saying that," Ally said. "But I'm not sure my parents would see it the same way. Anyway, just to be safe, I'd better power you down anytime we're around humans. Especially tonight—at the gala."

When Ally arrived at the diner for the gala, Flo and Randy were busy setting up. They'd placed little vases shaped like rocket ships on the tables and hung up a giant sign: Welcome, League of Rocket Scientists!
"It looks awesome in here!" Ally exclaimed.
"You haven't seen the best part." Flo nudged Randy. "Show her what you made."
Randy retrieved a tray from the kitchen. "It's nothing really. I was just having some fun."
Ally looked at Randy's creations. "Wow, Randy! You've made meatballs look like planets and pastries look like telescopes and computers!"
"Wait until you see the cake he made!" Flo said.
"Not yet though," Randy said. "Let me put the finishing touches on it first."
"I can't wait," Ally said. "I'll go wash my hands in the restroom. Then I'll help you finish preparing the food and decorations, Flo."
By the time Ally returned to the dining room, Mateo had arrived.

"I left gifts all over town for Bethany," he was explaining to Randy and Flo. "So far she's found an action figure and a pack of Cosmic Quest trading cards. Hopefully she's on her way to the comics bookstore for her next present and clue."
"Where will the final clue lead her?" Flo asked.

"To the red heart sculpture," Mateo replied. "That's where I'll give her the T-shirt. But after she figures out the clue at the bookshop, she'll come here to find the clue in the bathroom. I'd better get out of here! I don't want her to find me until the end."
"Will you be back in time for the gala?" Ally asked.
"I hope so!" Mateo hurried out the back door just as Bethany came in the front.
"Oh, hi, Bethany!" Ally tried to act surprised to see Bethany. "What are you doing here?"
"I'm on a scavenger hunt," Bethany replied in a flat voice. "A clue led me here."
"What is it?" Ally asked.
Bethany recited Mateo's riddle: "'Give me a tap and I'll give you some suds. I come in handy when you're covered in mud.'" Then she added sadly, "The answer is soap."
Ally peered at her. "Are you okay?"
Bethany shrugged and headed for the restroom.
"Huh," Ally thought. "She seems upset."
Ally did a quick scan of Bethany's mind. "Oh no!" Ally thought. "Bethany is upset about something—she thinks Mateo likes me! This is terrible!"
Ally paced around. When Bethany came out, Ally had to find a way to reassure her that Mateo and Ally were just good friends.
But before Bethany was back, Ray called Ally into the kitchen. And by the time Ally was finished helping him stack water glasses, Bethany was gone.
Ally stared at the diner entrance. "Why are humans so complicated?" she thought. "If they could read minds like Astralians, I wouldn't have to explain things to Bethany—she'd already know the truth!"
"What's the matter, hon?" Flo asked. "Is something bothering you?"
"There is. I—"
"Tonight's going to be epic!" Barry cried, bursting into the diner.
Ally scowled at him. "I know you wanted to try out the plate levitation trick tonight, Barry. But please don't. This night is too important to Ray."
Barry gave her a thumbs-up. "Got it."
"Go on, Ally," Flo said. "What were you saying?"
Ally didn't want to talk about her problems in front of Barry, but she needed advice about Bethany.
"I know! I'll ask Alpha!" Ally thought.
"It's nothing, Flo, thanks," Ally said. "I'm going to fix my hair before the gala begins."
Ally ducked into the restroom and reached into her apron pocket. But Alpha wasn't there! Ally checked everywhere. She checked the floor under the sink and next to the toilet.
Alpha was gone. Again!
"Maybe I dropped her in the dining room!" Ally raced out of the restroom to search for Alpha. But the gala guests had begun to arrive. There was no way Ally could search for Alpha now.
"I can't even listen for Alpha's strange noises because I powered her down," she thought. "Now what?"
"Ally!" Randy waved her into the kitchen and handed her a tray of appetizers. "Pass around these Cosmic Crescents. They're puff pastry filled with spinach and cheese."

Ally knew the gala was very important to Ray; it needed to go perfectly. But she was having a hard time keeping her mind on her job. As she wound her way through the guests, passing out food, she sneaked peeks under tables and in corners.
"Alpha has to be somewhere in the diner," Ally thought.
Once the tray of Cosmic Crescents was empty, Ally went back to the kitchen for another tray.
"These are Spinning Suns," Randy said. "They're mini pizzas with cheese and yellow peppers. Please tell people to be careful—they're hot."
Ally had just begun to pass out the Spinning Suns when something underneath a table caught her eye. It was small and shiny—just like the device!

Still holding the tray, Ally rushed across the diner. But she was so focused on the object under the table, she wasn't looking where she was going. Boom! She slammed into a tall gentleman who'd just entered the diner, and the tray of hot Spinning Suns flew out of her hand.
Ally quickly activated her levitation powers and stopped the tray just before it hit the floor. She grabbed the tray and turned to him. "Sorry, sir. I didn't see you there."

The man smiled. "That was amazing, young lady! I've heard such wonderful things about your tricks. So when the League of Rocket Scientists invited me to be their keynote speaker, I knew I had to come tonight."
"He's the president!" Ally thought as the man walked away. "And that was a close call!"
She quickly glanced under the table to look for Alpha.
"Ugh," she thought. The shiny object was someone's phone, not the device.
While the guests ate and the president gave his speech, Ally took every chance she had to look for Alpha.
"I can't believe I lost her a second time," Ally scolded herself. "I'm glad my parents aren't here—they'd be so disappointed in me."
"Ally, it's almost time to present Randy's rocket ship cake," Flo said. "As soon as the president finishes his speech, you can carry it out."
Ally went into the kitchen to get the cake, but Barry was already carrying the elaborately decorated cake.
"Be careful," Ally warned. "No tricks."
"Don't worry," Barry said. "This is going to be perfect!"
As soon as Barry stepped into the dining room with the rocket ship cake, the guests exploded into applause.
"That looks so real," one said.
"I can't believe we can eat that!" another said.

Ally held her breath as Barry made it all the way across the dining room with the cake. He was just about to set it down in front of the president when he tripped. The cake flew up—and landed right in the president's lap!
The room went silent as Barry stood there looking shocked, a broken spring dangling from his finger.
"Look at what you've done!" the president shouted at Barry.
"I'm sorry!" Barry said. "I just wanted to make you proud, Dad."
" Dad ?" Ally thought. "No wonder Barry has been trying to learn all about me! He's been spying on me for his father!"
