"Hi, Coach. I thought you said your brother owns this shop," Ally said.

The man laughed. "People always mix up my brother and me! I'm Eli, Coach Cross' brother. You must be Ally and Mateo. I'll be right with you kids. I just have to make some copies for another customer."
Eli started up one of the shop's large copy machines. The machine was so loud, Ally could hardly hear her own thoughts.
Eli came back to the counter. "I'm happy to help with your fundraiser. If you pay for the T-shirts and supply the design, I'll donate the cost of printing the shirts."
"That's very generous of you," Mateo said loudly. "How much are the T-shirts?"
"Five dollars each if you order between twenty and fifty shirts."
Eli started to punch numbers into his calculator, but Ally already had the math figured out.
"So, if we print fifty T-shirts, and charge fifteen dollars per shirt, we'll make over seven hundred dollars," she said.
"Minus the $250 you'll have to pay now to buy the T-shirts," Eli reminded her.
"But we don't have $250." Mateo sighed.
Ally pulled out her purse. "Yes, we do! I have a lot of money saved."
"Great, I'll start the paperwork," Eli said.
Mateo pulled Ally aside. "I can't ask you to pay for this, Ally."
"But you're not asking me to pay, Mateo. I'm offering. Besides, I might as well spend my Earth money now, since it will do me no good once I head back to space with Lainie."
Mateo grinned. "I didn't think of that! Thanks a lot. It's very nice of you to put the money down for us."
"No problem!" Ally set the bills on the floor.
Eli and Mateo looked at each other, confused.
"Um, Ally, what are you doing?" Mateo asked.
"You said to put the money down, so I did."
Eli and Mateo laughed.
"What's so funny?" Ally asked.
"Putting money down is just an expression," Mateo said. "It means to pay for something."
"Oh! I get it." Ally laughed as she picked the money up and handed it to Eli.
"Great," he said. "Send me your design as soon as you can. I need only a day or two to print the shirts."
"Thanks so much, Eli!" Mateo and Ally turned to leave when a dark-haired woman entered the shop. Her arms were full of blueprints.
"Hello, Mateo," the woman said. "It's so nice to see you."
"Hello, Mayor Clark," Mateo said.
"You must be Ally," the mayor said. "I've eaten at Ray's Diner many times, but you're always so busy, I've never had the chance to meet you. I just love all you've done for the diner."
"That's very nice of you to say," Ally said.

"That Gourmet Greta review brought a lot of positive attention to the town, and so many new tourists. And now Lainie Polk's launch is set to bring even more people here! In many ways, the plans in these blueprints are happening thanks to you, Ally."
Ally grinned proudly.
"Just wait until my parents hear about this," she thought. "They will be so impressed to hear that even the mayor was thankful for all I did on Earth!"
"Madam Mayor, what are the plans for?" Mateo asked. Just then his phone rang. "Oh, excuse me for a moment, this is my friend Bethany on the phone."
"Of course." Mayor Clark set her blueprints on the counter and started talking to Eli about making copies of them.
Between Mateo's talking on the phone and the noise of the copy machines, Ally wasn't sure she heard right. But she thought she heard the mayor say "soccer field."
She tried to read the mayor's mind, but the shop was still too noisy.
"I must have misheard her," Ally thought. "Why would an important person like the mayor of Sandville be thinking about a kids' soccer field?"
Mateo disconnected his call. "Hey, Ally, Bethany and Kate want us to meet them at the park. They have a design for the T-shirt, and a big surprise!"
"Sounds great!" Ally said. "Let's go!"
"Now is the time," Ally thought as she and Mateo walked to the park to meet Kate and Bethany. "As soon as I see Kate, I'm going to tell her the truth about my phone."
But when they found the girls, Kate was so excited about her T-shirt design, Ally didn't want to interrupt her.
"See?" Kate held out her tablet. "It's a soccer ball that's been kicked high up into the atmosphere and is circling the sun—like a planet."
"Isn't it stellar?" Bethany asked.
"It's amazing," Ally said.
"Can we add the words Sandville Soccer Club on the back of the shirts?" Mateo asked.
"Sure," Kate said. "And I'll make the letter o in Soccer Club look like a soccer ball."
"Can you send the design to me? I'll send it to the print shop," Mateo said.
"Sure." Kate made some quick changes to the design and sent it to Mateo.
"These T-shirts are going to sell like hotcakes!" Mateo said as he forwarded the design to Eli.
Ally frowned. "I hope they sell better than that! Pancakes are not one of the diner's top sellers."
Mateo, Bethany, and Kate laughed.
"You're so funny, Ally!" Kate said. "I have the best surprise for you. I bet you'll never guess what happened."
Bethany grinned. "You'll never guess!"
"What happened?" Ally asked.
"No, you have to guess," Kate said.
"I thought you said I'd never guess." Ally was confused. "Never is a very long time. It's almost as infinite as the universe."
It was Kate and Bethany's turn to be confused.
"Maybe you should just tell us, Kate," Mateo said quickly.
"I found your phone!" Kate cried.
"You did?" Ally blinked in surprise and touched her back pocket. Alpha was safely tucked away there. And luckily, she was staying quiet.
"Tell her how it happened, Kate," Bethany said.

Kate pulled an old phone that looked exactly like Alpha from her bag. "I was putting up signs near the diner. When I looked down, I spotted the phone just lying on the ground. It must have fallen out of your pocket one day. If it wasn't so old, someone else would have picked it up. Here you go!"
"Gosh, thanks so much." Ally flushed. How could she explain her fib now?
"Power it up. Make sure it still works," Bethany said.
"I hope it does. I love the funny things it says!" Kate grinned.
Ally gulped and pressed the Power button. The device lit up instantly.
"What do you think it will say first?" Kate asked eagerly.
"Um . . . er . . . ," Ally fumbled for words. "I don't think this phone is working—"
"Of course I'm working!" Alpha blurted out.
"Wow!" Kate laughed. "That app is amazing. The voice sounds like it's coming from your back pocket."
"Ha-ha! Really?" Ally reached around to her back pocket to try to turn Alpha off. But as Ally pulled her out, Alpha fell to the ground.
"Oh no!" Ally thought, looking down in horror.
"Wait, you have your phone?" Kate frowned.
"I, uh, didn't want to tell you, but I, well, I . . . bought another phone." As soon as the words came out of her mouth, Ally wanted to take them back. She had just told another fib!
"You did?" Kate asked. "Why? I told you I'd help you find your old phone."
"I know," Ally said in a rush. "But I didn't want to bother you. And besides, the old one isn't working so well."
"I'm working just fine!" Alpha snapped. "I can't believe you replaced me!"
Kate and Bethany cracked up, laughing.
But Ally wanted to cry. "This is awful," she thought. "My little fibs are spiraling out of control!"
"Oh, look at the time!" Mateo said, quickly checking his phone. "Ally and I have to get home to help my dad with something. Thanks again for the design, Kate!"
As they hurried away, Ally looked at him. "What do we need to help Ray with?"
"Nothing," Mateo said. "I just said that as an excuse to get away before things got worse."
Ally blinked. "You mean, you told a fib?"
"I guess." Mateo shrugged. "It was harmless, and you needed help. No one was going to get hurt because I said it."
Ally shook her head. "So, on Earth it's okay to tell a fib if it doesn't hurt anyone?"
"Yep," Mateo said.
"Phew!" Relief washed over Ally. "That's great news!" Now she didn't have to tell Kate the truth!
The next morning Ally overslept. "Ack! I'm late for work!" She jumped out of bed. "Alpha, why didn't you wake me up as always?"
Alpha made a snorting sound. "Ask your other phone to wake you up!"
"I don't have another phone," Ally tried to say, but Alpha had shut herself down.
At work, Barry had taken all the customers' orders.
"Thanks for covering for me," Ally said.
"No problem," Barry said. "I heard about your fundraiser for the soccer club. I'd love to help. Maybe I can cook something for you to sell?"

"We're selling T-shirts, but thanks anyway." Ally started to refill the saltshakers when she got an idea. "Actually, I could use your help with something else. Can you meet me at Ray's house tonight?"
"Sure!" Barry looked so happy to be included, Ally couldn't help smiling too.
Later Ally went to the print shop to look at some sample soccer T-shirts.
"These look amazing, Eli!" Ally said.
"Great. I'll start printing the rest of them right now," Eli said.
Ally slipped one of the T-shirts over her clothes. "I can't wait to show Mateo! See you later. Thanks."
Outside, she ran into Mayor Clark.
"Nice T-shirt. Did Eli make that for you?" the mayor asked.
"Yes. We're going to sell them to raise money for a soccer club."
"Where will the club meet?" Mayor Clark asked.
"At the soccer field in town," Ally said.
"Oh!" The mayor got a funny look on her face. "The city just signed a contract with a developer. We're going to turn that field into a parking lot."
"What?" Ally gasped. "Why?"
"With more tourists coming to Sandville—thanks in large part to you, Ally—we need more parking lots. I've got a meeting. Nice to see you!"
Ally stared after the mayor.

"What have I done?" she thought. "I helped Sandville but totally wrecked Mateo's soccer club dreams! I can't believe the field is going to be destroyed. And Eli is about to print a bunch more T-shirts!"
Ally raced back to the shop to stop the order. But there was an Out to Lunch sign on the door.
Ally reached for Alpha. Maybe she could call the shop and leave a message for Eli. But she'd left Alpha—who was really mad at her—at home.
Ally groaned. "I'd better go tell Mateo about all this."
Ally raced to the soccer field as fast as she could. When she got there, Coach and Mateo were on the field.
"I dread telling them the bad news," Ally thought.
"Hey, are you space girl?" someone called.
Ally spun around. A boy, another soccer player, stood grinning at her.
"Oh no!" Ally thought. "He knows I'm an alien!"
"Hi, I'm Julius. You're the one who won the spot on Lainie Polk's P.O.D., right?"
Ally laughed from relief. "Yes!"
"It's so cool," Julius said. "You'll have to tell me all about space when you get back."
"Oh, I . . ." Ally was stumped. She couldn't tell him she wasn't coming back to Earth. Then she remembered what Mateo had said about fibs. They weren’t bad if no one got hurt.
"Sure! I'll tell you all about space. Right now I'm waiting for Mateo. I have to tell him something. It's not about space, though."
Julius pointed to a bench. "You can wait there. He'll be done soon."
Ally blushed as Julius flashed her another smile. "His eyes are so blue," she thought.
Soon Mateo and Coach trotted off the field.
Mateo smiled when he saw Ally's shirt. "The T-shirt looks great!"
"Yes, but . . ." Ally told them about her conversation with Mayor Clark.
Mateo gasped. "This is terrible!"
"Good thing you didn't get all the T-shirts printed," Coach said.
Ally explained how she tried to cancel the print job, but Eli was out to lunch.

"Excuse me." Julius stepped closer. "I couldn't help but overhear you. Don't cancel those T-shirts—we need to fight for our soccer field. And those shirts are a great way for Sandville residents to support us."
"I agree!" Mateo said.
"We could also write letters to the mayor," Julius said.
"Maybe we could get people to sign a petition too," Mateo said.
"Everyone at soccer camp will help us get signatures," Julius said.
Ally grinned. "Let's do it! I really want to fix this before I leave for home—I mean, leave for space—with Lainie Polk!"
That evening Ally, Mateo, Bethany, Kate, and Julius gathered at Ray's house to start writing letters to the mayor.
"It was nice of your dad to let us come here to write letters," Julius said.
"He loves having people over," Mateo said. "He said he and Flo will write letters later, after they get back from seeing a movie. And he'll buy five T-shirts too!"
"Woo-hoo!" Ally said.
"I've texted everyone I know, asking them to text everyone they know to write letters," Kate said. "I told them we're making a petition too."
"What do you think of this?" Bethany held up a banner she was making: "Soccer Fields Are More Important than Parking Lots!"
"That's so great!" Mateo gushed.
"I can't wait until the post office starts delivering all these letters to the mayor's office," Julius said.
"I was thinking I could bring some of them to the mayor," Ally said. "Maybe I can convince her to stop the construction plans when I'm there."
"It's worth a try," Mateo said. "You can be very convincing, Ally."
"Sometimes I'm too convincing," Ally thought. "If I hadn't helped Sandville grow so quickly, the mayor wouldn't be turning the soccer field into a parking lot."
Just then the doorbell rang.
"I'll get it." Ally answered the door.
It was Barry.
"Oh no!" Ally thought. "I forgot! I asked him to come over to help me plan Mateo's Holly Days party!"
"Hi, Barry! Did you come to help us write letters?" Ally gave him a big wink so he'd know to play along.
But of course Barry didn't get it.
"Don't you remember?" he asked with a frown. "You asked me to come over so we could talk about something."
"Shh!" Ally whispered. "That's a surprise. Just play along!"
"Oh, right!" Barry said loudly. "I definitely came here to write letters, lots and lots of letters."
"Phew!" Ally thought. "He finally understood that I was telling a good fib."
A few hours later, the kids had a stack of letters and several posters ready to hang up around town. They'd also prepared the petition.
"Let's meet at the field tomorrow. We'll have the T-shirts then," Mateo said.
"We can also collect signatures on the petition and get more people to write letters," Bethany said.
"Great plan." Julius nodded.
Soon Mateo offered to walk Bethany and Kate home.
"And, uh, I can stay and help you finish cleaning up, Ally," Julius said.
"That's very nice of you," Ally said quickly. "But Barry will help me."
"I will?" Barry asked. Ally winked at him again, and he added, "Oh, yeah, I will!"
"Okay, well, good night then." Julius looked disappointed as he left.
Ally sighed. "I think I just hurt his feelings," she thought. "Too bad I'm leaving soon. I'd really like to get to know him better."
"So, what do you need help with?" Barry asked.
Ally explained her plan to throw a party celebrating all the Holly Days at once for Mateo. "I want to serve all the traditional foods. It'll be a giant feast!"
Barry laughed. "That sounds like fun. I'll be happy to make the food. This will be a good chance to show Ray I can do more than wait tables."
"Great! Here's the menu I was thinking of." Ally handed Barry a list of dishes she wanted to serve.

"Let's see what you've got." Barry read the list out loud. "'Roasted turkey with chocolate sauce, ham with candy eggs, potato pancakes with gravy, and sweet potatoes with rice cakes.' This menu is, er, interesting. But I'll do whatever you ask!"
After Barry left, Ally went into her room and booted up Alpha.
"Hi, Alpha! Let's play some quiet music."
"Why don't you ask your other phone," Alpha said.
"There is no other phone!" Ally said.
"Then what is this device next to me?" Alpha asked.
"Well, it's another phone, but I only have it because Kate gave it to me."
"Illogical. You have another phone."
"But I only have it because I told Kate that I'd lost you. It was a harmless fib."
" Harmless and fib are incompatible words," Alpha snapped.
"Not always," Ally said. "Mateo said it's okay to fib on Earth as long as no one gets hurt."
"Harumph! I guess you consider me no one then!" Alpha's screen went black as she turned herself off.
"Are you ready to sell some T-shirts?" Ally asked Mateo as they carried boxes onto the soccer field the next day. They had just picked up the T-shirts from the print shop.
"I sure am," Mateo said.
Ally looked at the field. "I hope lots of people show up to help out."
"I don't think we have to worry about that." Mateo grinned. "Look at the field!"
Kate and Bethany were there. And so was Barry, along with everyone from soccer camp. On the opposite side of the field, Ally saw even more people.

"It looks like those people are already collecting signatures for our petition!" Ally smiled. "Kate did a great job spreading the word around town. I'm so happy this many people showed up to save the soccer field."
"Uh, I'm not sure that's why everyone is here," Mateo said.
Ally followed his gaze across the field. Those people were wearing T-shirts too. But theirs read People for More Parking.

Ally frowned. "Why would anyone want a parking lot more than a soccer field?" Then her face lit up. "I'm going to talk to them! I'll use my Astralian powers to convince them that Sandville needs to keep this soccer field."
Ally hurried over to a man who was collecting signatures for the parking lot. She asked why he wanted a new parking lot.
"Since more tourists started coming to town, it's become impossible to find a parking spot." The man scowled. "Customers can't come to our stores. We can't park to run errands. It's a nightmare!"
"I didn't think of all that," Ally said. "But having a place for people to play soccer is important too."

"You can't have everything, kid," the man said. "We'll just have to see which side collects more signatures. But I doubt it will be your side. We already have more than two hundred signatures from Sandville residents."
Ally gasped. More than two hundred signatures?

"I guess we lost," she thought as she headed back to her friends. "I thought I'd be able to go home and tell my parents about all the great things I did in Sandville. But now I'll have to go home and admit I messed things up."
"Ally, what did that man say?" Barry asked.
Ally shook her head. "That we'll have to see which side can collect more signatures. And they already have over two hundred!"
Julius shrugged. "Then I guess we'd better get to work."
"You think we can get more signatures than they got?" Ally asked.
"We'll never know if we don't try," Julius said.
"Julius is right," Mateo said. "Let's fan out around town and get as many signatures as we can."
The soccer kids broke up into small groups and headed into town. Soon the only people left at the field were Ally, Barry, and Julius.
Julius' cheeks turned pink. "Do you want to go to the UFO Museum with me to collect signatures, Ally?"
Ally wasn't trying to read his mind, but she could sense something strong. "He likes me," she thought. "It's the same feeling that Mateo had for Bethany before they'd started dating."
And she liked him back. "But I'm leaving soon and never coming back," Ally thought. "I can't explain that, and I don't want to fib again."
"Um," Ally fumbled for words. "I, um, no thanks. Barry's going to the diner to collect signatures. I think I'll just go there too."
Julius looked hurt. "See you later," he mumbled as he walked away.
"Ugh!" Ally thought in frustration. "I hurt his feelings again . . . maybe this time I should have told a fib!"
"Are you ready to go collect signatures, Ally?" Barry asked.
"Sure." Ally sighed.
While Ally and Barry collected signatures outside the diner, they talked about the menu for Ally's surprise Holly Days party.
"This is going to be an unusual party," Barry said.
"That's for sure!" Ally laughed.
"Barry! Can you come here, please?" Ray called Barry into the diner.
A few minutes later, Barry was back.
"What was that about?" Ally asked.
"It was about me saving your party."
"Huh? What do you mean?"
Barry grinned proudly. "Ray heard us talking about a surprise party. He asked me who was throwing one, so I told him someone called to book a party here. Good idea, right?"
"What?" Ally slapped her forehead. "No, Barry! That was a terrible idea! Now Ray thinks he has to cook and shop for a party that's not real!"

Ally raced into the diner, determined to not let another fib get out of control. She had to explain to Ray that there had been a misunderstanding about the surprise party. But Ray was busy talking on the phone.
"I don't want to interrupt him," Ally thought. "I'll explain all this later at home."
After she and Barry were done collecting signatures for the petition, Ally headed home.
"Alpha is still mad at me. I have to talk to her about things too," Ally thought.
In her room she booted Alpha up. "Hi, Alpha, I'm home."
Alpha made a snorting sound.
"I know you're still mad at me, and I'm really sorry," Ally said. "The fibs I've told have gotten out of control and caused lots of trouble."
"Humans fib because they can. They do not possess mind-reading abilities like Astralians," Alpha said. "Fibs can easily get out of control."
"I know that now," Ally said. "I thought if no one got hurt, then telling fibs wasn't a bad thing. But I realize you can't always know who your fibs will hurt."
"Affirmative." Alpha's tone softened. "It is clear you meant well. However, logic dictates you must tell the truth to everyone you have fibbed to."
Ally nodded. "Let's see . . . Who have I fibbed to? Kate, Julius, Ray, sort of, and this doesn't even include all the people I've hidden my real identity from—"
"Correction," Alpha interrupted. "It would be unwise to expose your Astralian identity."
"But isn't pretending to be human a kind of fib?"
"There are some truths that could endanger you. Some fibs are told out of necessity, but you must choose wisely."
Ally groaned. "I'm still confused, but maybe that's what Mateo meant when he said some fibs are harmless."
"Affirmative."

"Thank you for helping me, Alpha. Okay, I'm going to do it! I'm going to tell the truth to everyone I've fibbed to. But first I have to bring the letters to Mayor Clark and try to fix this mess with the soccer field."
Ally was about to put Alpha in her pocket when she noticed she had a voicemail message.
"Oh! Lainie called today," Ally said. "She finally called me back."
Ally hit Play.
"Hi, Ally. Please call me back about the P.O.D. as soon as you can."
"Quick, Alpha," Ally commanded. "Call Lainie."
The phone rang twice before the call went to Lainie's voicemail.
Ally left a message. "Hi, Lainie. I'm sorry I missed your call. Please call me back as soon as you can. I'm so excited to blast off with you!"
Ally hung up and got ready to head into town. "It's time to get back to work!"
Ally arrived at the mayor's office a little while later.
"May I please speak with the mayor?" Ally asked the mayor's assistant.
"She's in a meeting," the assistant said.
"I can wait," Ally said. "It's very important."
Ally waited for almost an hour before the mayor's door opened. Mayor Clark walked out with two men carrying blueprints.
"We're excited for you to get to work!" she said to the men.
The men handed her the blueprints and left.
"Wait!" Ally jumped up. "Were you talking about the parking lot? Because we collected a lot of letters and signatures on a petition. Lots of people want to save the soccer field."
"I know. We're getting a lot of phone calls in support of the field. But I'm sorry, Ally, it's too late." Mayor Clark shook her head.
"But the kids will lose their soccer field!" Ally said.
The mayor shrugged sadly. "It's life, I suppose." She turned to go back to her office when Ally's eyes landed on the blueprints.
"Are those the plans for the parking lot?" she asked. "May I look at them?"

"I don't see why not." The mayor spread the blueprints out on a table. "Here's the parking lot. And we've planned for a small drive-through coffee shop so people can grab a cup of coffee on their way to work. I was going to ask Ray if he'd like to run it."
Ally's eyes went wide. She had just gotten the best idea!

"Mayor, did you know that Ray has a food truck? What if he agreed to serve coffee and breakfast foods every morning? Then you won't have to build the shop, and the parking lot could be smaller, leaving room for a field."
The mayor frowned.
Ally held her breath. "Please, please, please," she thought.

"You know . . ." The mayor looked thoughtful. "That's not a bad idea." She rolled up the blueprints. "Maybe I'll speak to the developers to see what they think. Do you want to speak with Ray about the coffee?"
"Of course!"
Ally left the office and crossed her fingers. But it wasn't because she had told a fib. This time it was for luck that her plan would work!
Ally couldn't wait to ask Ray about the coffee truck. But first she had some apologies to make.
Outside the mayor's office, she called Kate.
"I have to tell you something," Ally said. "I didn't lose my phone. I just didn't want you asking to see my phone all the time. I'm so sorry I fibbed!"
Kate was quiet. Ally was scared that Kate was mad, but then Kate laughed.
"I get it. I don't like it when friends keep asking to borrow my clothes. I promise to stop asking. And I'll put up signs to find the other phone's owner."
"Great!" Ally said. "Also, can you help me with something?"
"Sure!"
Ally told Kate about the surprise Holly Days party. "It's tonight. Can you make sure Mateo comes home at exactly six?"
"No problem!"
Ally got Julius' number from Kate. Then she called him to apologize for hurting his feelings twice. "It's been a rough week, but I'd really like to be friends. Can you forgive me?"
Julius stayed quiet too.
"He hates me," Ally thought.
"I understand," Julius said softly. "Thanks for telling me."
Ally told Julius about the party and invited him.
"See you then!" Julius said.
"I'll make my next apology in person," Ally thought, heading to the diner.
Ray was in the office.
"Hi, Ally! I was just thinking about that surprise party. I'll need to order food. Do you know what menu they want?"
"Uh, Ray, there is no surprise party. At least not here. Barry was helping me plan something for Mateo. I wanted to explain, but you were on the phone and . . ."
Ray looked confused, but he nodded. "Okay, no big deal. But why are you throwing Mateo a party? It's not his birthday."
"I wanted to do something nice for him before I go to space." Ally explained her idea. "It's just a few friends coming over tonight. Is that okay?"
"Sure."
"I have another exciting thing to ask you." Ally told Ray about her idea.
"A coffee food truck sounds great, but I don't have anyone who can run it," Ray said.
"Oh yes you do!" Ally said.
Ally was decorating for the Holly Days party when the doorbell rang.
"Wow, it looks great in here!" Barry said, carrying in food.
"Thanks!"
Soon everything was laid out on the table.
"Great job, Barry. It looks delicious!"
"Your mixed-up menu was fun to make," Barry said. "I hope Ray likes it too."
"Me too," Ally said. "I can't wait for Mateo and everyone to get here."
Soon the front door opened. In came Ray, Flo, Kate, Bethany, Julius, and Mateo.
"Happy Holly Days!" Ally cried.
"Wow!" Mateo looked around. "You remembered how much I love the holidays!"
"Yes! And now, I don't have to miss any when I go to—uh, space!" Ally said.
"I can't believe you did all this on your own," Mateo said.
"Barry helped," Ally said. "We planned the menu together, but he cooked everything."
"Oh! The menu is surprising, but it looks delicious!" Ray said.
Ally pulled Ray aside. "What do you think about my food truck idea now?"
"I agree! Let's ask Barry to run it," Ray said. "Thanks to you, I see he's a good cook."
Ally beamed. "Soon I'll be telling my parents all about my good deeds," she thought.
"Everyone, dig in!" Ally called. She started to fill her own plate with food when her phone buzzed. It was Lainie.
"I'm calling to tell you some news, Ally. I'm canceling the launch."
"What?" Ally's heart sank.
"You were right," Lainie said. "Saving endangered species is a much better use of my money than exploring space. So, I'm investing in a wildlife refuge. Gotta go! Bye!"
"Oh no," Ally thought. "I was so close to going back home, and now . . ." She stood there, trying not to cry.
Then someone hurried to her side.
"Ally, are you all right?" Julius asked.
Ally blinked back tears. "Lainie canceled the launch!"
"I'm so sorry," Julius said. "I, um, know this isn't as cool as going to space, but would you maybe . . . want to go to the movies with me sometime?"
"I'd love to!" Ally burst out.
Julius grinned at her, and she smiled back.
"It's not all bad news," she thought. "Because of me, Lainie is going to save endangered species. I get to spend more time with my friends. And I have a movie date—with a very cute Earthling!"

51.title: Who Wants to Be on TV?

paragraphs.text: It was a quiet morning at Ray's Diner. Flo was helping Randy in the kitchen while Ally was refilling saltshakers. But she wasn't doing a very good job.
"Oh no." Ally moaned. "This is the third time I overfilled a shaker!" She began cleaning up the mess. "I have to keep my mind on my work and stop thinking about—"
Mateo burst into the diner. "Hey, Ally!"
"Ahh!" Ally was so startled, she spilled even more salt!
"Oops, sorry to scare you," Mateo said. "I'm just really excited! Aren't you?"
Ally sighed. "What is there to be excited about?"
"The lunar eclipse on Saturday night! Remember? I sent you that article about it."
"Oh, right." Ally shrugged and went back to cleaning up the salt.
"I thought you'd be excited to see the lunar eclipse and . . ." Mateo trailed off, peering closely at her. "Oh. It reminds you of home, is that it?"
"No, we don't even have a moon," Ally said.
"Then what's wrong? You don't seem like yourself," Mateo said.
Ally looked at Mateo in confusion. "If I'm not myself, who would I be?"
"It's just an expression," Mateo said. "It means you're not acting like you usually do."

"Oh!" Ally blurted out what was bothering her. "I was so happy when Julius asked me to go to the movies with him. But I haven't heard from him since that night. I guess he changed his mind about our date."
"That's weird," Mateo said. "Because when I saw him two days ago, he said he was really looking forward to going on a date with you. Maybe he got cold feet."
Flo came into the dining room. "Who has cold feet?" she asked.
"Julius does," Ally said. "Mateo says that's why he hasn't called me to set up a date yet. But I don't know what the temperature of his feet has to do with anything."

Flo laughed. "He's probably just nervous, Ally. Maybe he thinks you changed your mind about the date. Hey! I have an idea! What if you go on a double date with Mateo and Bethany? That way neither of you will feel a lot of pressure. What do you think?"
Ally frowned. "A double date? How about a single date first?"
"A double date means two couples go out together," Mateo said.
"Silly me!" Ally giggled. "That's a great idea, Flo. That should make all our feet nice and warm!"
Ally was beginning to feel better when Barry ran into the diner.
"Have you heard of the TV show Food Truck Rally ?" he asked breathlessly.
"Sure," Mateo said.
"I haven't," Ally said. "What is it?"
"It's a reality show with food trucks," Barry said. "The idea is that six food trucks compete in a one-day cook-off around a theme. The winning truck gets five thousand dollars!"
"It sounds fun," Ally said.
Barry nodded. "Well, guess what. They picked Sandville as the location for a new episode. The theme is Out of This World, and they want Rolling Ray's to compete!"
"Papi is going to be thrilled!" Mateo said.
Barry nodded. "I hope so."
Just then Mateo's phone rang. "It's my dad. We'll find out right now what he thinks." He started a video call with Ray. "Hey, Papi. We have some exciting news!"
"I do too!" Ray said. "You go first."
Barry leaned in toward Mateo's phone. "Rolling Ray's has been invited to compete on the next episode of Food Truck Rally ."
"The prize is five thousand dollars," Mateo said.

Ray looked upset. "Gosh, kids, I'm sorry, I can't do it. I finally planned a vacation for myself—a fishing trip with my high school buddies. I leave tomorrow. Mateo, your mom will come and stay with you and Ally while I'm gone."
Mateo sighed. "Well, you deserve a vacation, Papi. I guess we have to turn the TV show down."
Barry looked upset.
"Maybe we don't have to say no," Ally said. "Barry has been running the food truck all by himself and doing a great job. Mateo, you and I can help him with the cook-off."
"Yeah!" Mateo nodded. "Bethany and Kate can probably help too."
"An all-kid team!" Barry said. "The show loves teams with a gimmick. And so do the fans."
"Great!" Ray smiled. "And if you win, you kids can split the prize."
"Wow," Ally said as Mateo hung up the call. "We're going to be on TV. I can't wait to be a star!"
Ally was still talking to Barry and Mateo about the cook-off.
"If we win the contest, I'm going to use my prize money for cooking classes," Barry said.
"And I'm going to buy a collector's edition of the first Cosmic Quest comic book. They're expensive!" Mateo said.
"What about you, Ally?" Barry asked.
Ally scratched her head. "I can't think of anything I need."
"I bet you'll come up with something," Barry said.
"So, tell us more about Food Truck Rally , Barry," Ally said.
"Yeah, what other local food trucks are going to be in the contest?" Mateo asked.
"They sent me a list." Barry pulled out his phone. "There's Taco Nation, Gimme the Beef, Ella's Eats, the Food Dude, and us."
"That's only five food trucks," Ally said. "You said that the contest was among six trucks."
"You're right." Barry scanned the list again. "Oh," he said, biting his lip. "I didn't see the last truck on the list."
"So, who is it?" Mateo asked.
Barry held up his phone.
"What?" Mateo's eyes went wide as he stared at the screen. "Pepe's? Since when do they have a food truck?"
Barry shrugged. "Their website says it's brand-new."

Ally's eyes flashed. "Pepe's almost cost Ray his business once! We cannot let them win. Barry, you should come up with something really fantastic to serve at the contest, something guaranteed to win!"
"Yeah," Mateo said. "Something that no one will be expecting."
"I'm already on it!" Barry hurried out of the diner.
"So, let's talk about our double date," Mateo said to Ally. "What do kids on Astralia do on dates?"
"Stardust catching is really popular," Ally said. "We wear special spacesuits and collect stardust."
"That sounds like fun," Mateo said. "But we've got too much gravity here on Earth to go stardust catching."
"Are you going to take my advice and plan a double date?" Flo asked as she came out of the kitchen.
Ally nodded. "We're trying to think of what to do."

"What about going to the park on Saturday night to watch the lunar eclipse? You can have a picnic," Flo said. She looked up as two customers walked into the diner. "You stay here, Ally. I'll get their order."
"Thanks, Flo," Ally said.
"I'm always here for you, Ally." Flo hurried off.
"I like Flo's idea," Mateo said. "Ally, you should just call Julius. Girls ask boys out on dates all the time here."
"We do too on Astralia, but I don't have time to spend a full day serenading him in public."
"Huh?" Mateo looked confused.
"That's what we do on Astralia," Ally said. "We follow the person around and sing their favorite songs to them all day long."
"That sounds like a lot," Mateo said. "Calling him might be easier."
Ally gulped, suddenly worried. "What if he's changed his mind about me? Or maybe he figured out that I'm an alien! Do you think he'd tell Dr. Lloyd?"
"You're being silly," Mateo said.
"Okay, I'll do it." Ally pulled Alpha out of her pocket and powered her up. "Alpha, call Julius."
Alpha made a snorting sound. "Fine."
Ally held her breath, waiting for Julius to answer. But after one ring, the line went dead.
"That's strange," Ally said. "Alpha, call Julius."
Again, the phone rang once and went dead.
Ally tried two more times and then gave up. "He doesn't want to talk to me."
Mateo shook his head. "It's probably just Alpha glitching again. Try calling him with my phone."
Ally hesitated.
"Do you want me to call him?" Mateo asked.
"No, that's silly," Ally said. "I'll do it, but after work and at home, in private. Maybe I'll be less nervous then."
But later, Ally felt just as anxious. She paced around her room with Mateo's phone in her hand.
"I don't know why I'm so nervous, Alpha. It's just a phone call. But what if he picks up this time and I don't know what to say?"
"Preparation is the key to any task," Alpha said.
"You're right, Alpha! I'm glad to see you working perfectly now. That gives me a good idea. Write me a script of what to say to Julius."
Alpha growled. "I am not a toy!"
"I know," Ally said. "But your prime directive is to assist me."
"Fine." Alpha grumbled.
A short script appeared on the screen.
"Thank you!" Ally said. "I'm finally ready to make this call!"
Ally held her breath. Julius' phone rang once, twice, then . . .
"Hey, Mateo!" Julius said. "You reached me while I was reading a good spy novel. What's up?"
"Uh . . ." Ally fumbled to read the script on Alpha's screen. "Hello, Julius. This is Allyzooba of Astralia, east of the Milky . . ." Her voice trailed off.
"Eek! Alpha's script is terrible!" Ally thought.
"Ally?" Julius sounded concerned. "Are you okay?"
"I, er . . . I was wondering if you'd want to . . ." Ally flushed. "I mean you don't have to, no pressure. Oh, maybe this was a bad idea. I bet you were just being nice, right?"
"Nice about what?" Julius asked.
"About going on a date." Ally paused, and then added, "With me."
There was a long silence.
Ally started to sweat. "I knew it was a bad idea to ask you!"
"Not at all!" Julius said. "I'm sorry, I just didn't know what to say. I've been trying to call you. But you haven't answered my calls. I thought you didn't want to talk to me."
"Really? I . . ." Ally looked down at Alpha and guessed what had happened—Alpha still wasn't working right.
"I'm sorry," she said. "My phone is, er, unreliable."
"I understand," Julius said. "Anyway, I'd love to go a date with you."
"You would?" Ally smiled. "That's great! Mateo suggested that we go on a double date to watch the eclipse on Saturday night."
"That sounds cool," Julius said. "Should we meet in the park at seven?"
"Yes! See you then!" Ally hung up the phone. She was so happy, she didn't even feel mad at Alpha for messing up the script.
"Alpha, play some music. I want to dance!"
"Harumph!" Alpha snorted and shut herself off.
Ally shook her head. "Alpha's acting so weird," she thought. "Almost as if she doesn't like Julius or something. Hmm. Can computers get jealous?"
The next day Ally was working at the counter while Flo was in the kitchen helping Randy.
Barry rushed over. "I know what to serve for the food truck contest! I bet no one else will have it at their truck!"
"What is it?" Ally said.
"It's a surprise!" Barry said. "I'm going into the kitchen now to try it out."
"I can't wait to see what it is," Ally said.
Two customers came in and sat at the counter.
"Can I get you something to drink?" Ally asked, handing them menus.
"We're not here to eat," the man said. "I'm Jerry. I'm a producer at Food Truck Rally . This is Sally, my cameraperson."
"Oh!" Ally smoothed her hair. "Am I on TV now?"
"Not yet." Jerry laughed. "Is Barry here?"
"He's in the kitchen. In fact, he's trying out a new recipe for the contest."

"Oh, good," Jerry said. "We want to get footage of all the food truck teams in the days leading up to the contest. You contestants signed legal forms to participate in the contest. But we need everyone to fill out another form. Can you ask the others to come out of the kitchen?"
"Sure! I'll get Barry, Randy, and Flo."
Randy and Barry came out first.
Jerry handed out sheets of paper. "Here are the waivers for you to sign."
Ally, Randy, and Barry signed them.
"Great!" Jerry said. "Now we can film you. Barry, can you tell the camera what you're working on?"

"Well, I was going to keep it a surprise, but I suppose I can reveal it to the camera." Barry smiled. "I call it my Out of This World Cosmic Club. It's turkey and avocado, topped by huevos rancheros and potato chips."
"That sounds like a winner to me!" Ally said.
"What's a winner?" Flo asked as she came out of the kitchen.
"Barry's sandwich for the contest," Ally said. "Here, Flo, you have to sign a waiver so the TV show can film you working."
"Oh no!" Flo's cheeks flushed as she covered her face with a menu. "I don't want to be on TV!"
"Really?" Ally was surprised. She thought everybody on Earth loved the idea of being on TV and becoming famous. "But you like to sing and make jokes and—"
"I said no!" Flo scurried back into the kitchen with the menu still covering her face.
"That was strange," Ally thought, confused.
She tried to read Flo's mind, but she could only hear one thought from Flo: "Get me out of here as fast as possible!"

54.title: Earth Girls Just Want to Have Fun

paragraphs.text: Later Ally and Flo were wiping tables.
Flo suddenly looked at her phone. "Do you mind if I leave now?"
"Sure," Ally said. "Is everything all right?"
"Yep! Thanks!" Flo hurried out of the diner.
"Boy, everything doesn't seem all right with her," Ally thought. "Something must be wrong. I'll ask her next time I see her."
Jerry and Sally came in a few minutes later.
Ally greeted them with a smile. "Are you here to film us again?"
"No," Jerry said. "We thought we'd grab a bite to eat."
"Well, you're in for a treat." Ally grinned. "I don't want to brag, but we're the best restaurant in town!"
Jerry and Sally sat down, and Ally brought them menus.
"This is going to be a fun episode of the show," Jerry said. "There are good teams in Sandville. But I think Pepe's is the one to beat."
"Ugh!" Ally thought.
"Well, we're not worried!" she said brightly. "Rolling Ray's is going to roll over all the competition!"
"They sure are!" someone said.
Ally spun around. Mateo's mother had just entered, followed by Kate and Bethany.
"Dawn, you're here!" Ally gave Dawn a hug.
"It's good to see you, Ally," Dawn said. "I ran into the girls on my way over here. They told me about the cook-off."
"And about our double date," Bethany said.
"What are you going to wear, Ally?" Kate asked.
"You should wear something cute but casual," Dawn said. "I have an idea! Why don't we all go shopping to find you a new outfit?"
"Sure, that sounds fun," Ally said. "I finish working soon."
"We'll get something to eat and wait for you," Dawn said.
They sat down, and Kate pulled out her phone.
"Hey, look." She showed everyone her screen. "Some of the other food trucks have begun announcing the dishes they'll be serving at the cook-off."
"Yum!" Bethany said. "Ella's Eats is going to serve a club sandwich with turkey, chips, a fried egg, and a spicy sauce."
"Spicy eggs?" Ally said. "With turkey and chips? Oh no! That sounds like Barry's new sandwich. He's going to have to come up with something else for our team."
"Ally?" Jerry waved her over. "Bad news. We just got a text and have to go. We'll take a rain check on eating here."
Ally scratched her head as they hurried out. "What does the rain have to do with anything?" she thought.
Later, after shopping with Dawn and her friends, Ally held up her new outfit.
"What do you think, Alpha?" Ally asked.
"I think a great many things," Alpha said. "I think we still have no way to get home. And I think . . ." She snorted. "Going on a date with a human is dangerous!"
Ally rolled her eyes. "I meant about my outfit. And you don't have to remind me all the time that we don't have a way home—yet. But don't worry, we'll get back to Astralia one day."
"One day on Earth is approximately 24 hours long. One year on Earth is—"
"You don't have to tell me how time works here on Earth either," Ally said. "But why do you think going on a date is dangerous? Julius is very nice."

"An Astralian's prime directive is to resolve conflicts and bring peace to the universe," Alpha said. "Not go on dates with Earthlings. You are getting distracted, Allyzooba, and becoming more and more like a human."
"That's not true," Ally snapped. "And I'll prove it. Humans can't throw their voices."
Ally looked out the window. There was a man walking a dog past the house.
"Cute dog!" Ally said, throwing her voice behind them.
"Huh?" The man looked confused. "Rover, did you hear that?"

"See?" Ally said gleefully. "I'm nothing like a human! Plus, I'm being very helpful on this planet. I'm helping Barry with the contest so he can take special cooking classes. I'm helping Mateo buy a rare comic book."
"Those are acceptable missions," Alpha mumbled. But she didn't sound very impressed.
"Thank you," Ally said. "Just don't forget that I'm allowed to have some fun on Earth while I'm helping humans and bringing peace to the universe."
"Fun?" Alpha snorted again. "Fun does not compute."
"Well, I hope it does for my date with Julius," Ally said. "Because I really like him, and I hope he likes me too!"
With that, Ally turned Alpha off and put away her new outfit.
The next morning, when Ally got to work, Randy and Flo were standing behind the counter speaking in low voices.
"Good morning," Ally said cheerfully.
"Oh, hi," Randy said.
But Flo barely greeted Ally before they both went back to work.
"That's odd," Ally thought, tying on her apron. "Are they mad at me? But why? Oh! Maybe Flo's upset that Ray went on vacation without her."
But that didn't feel right either. Flo and Ray hadn't been dating that long. Then it hit her.
"Flo is probably upset that Dawn is back," Ally thought.
Just then Jerry and Sally walked into the diner.
"Barry asked us to meet him here," Jerry said. "While we wait, we'd like to shoot some footage of the diner."
"No problem," Ally said. "Just don't film Flo."
Soon Barry arrived, grinning. "I came up with a new dish. It's guaranteed to be something no one else will have."
"You mean like Gorphelian Glug?" Ally asked.
Everyone gave Ally a strange look.
"Tee-hee!" Ally blushed. "Just kidding. What's your idea, Barry?"
"Crater Cakes!" Barry said proudly.
"What are those?" Randy asked.
"Peanut butter and marshmallow hand pies. I bet everyone else will be making main course dishes. While Rolling Ray's is the only one serving dessert!"
"That's a cool idea," Ally said.
"I'm going to the truck to make a test batch," Barry said.
"Mind if we come along?" Jerry asked. "We'd like to film you."
"Sure!" Barry said. "Let's go!"

At work, Ally didn't get a chance to ask Flo if something was wrong. As she walked into her room later, she told herself that she would try again soon. For now, she had to get ready for tonight's double date.
"Should I wear my hair in a ponytail or down?" Ally asked Alpha.
"Hair is for humans, not Astralians," Alpha said.
"I know, but I like having it." Ally started brushing her hair when a thought stopped her. "What if, once he gets to know me, Julius decides he doesn't like me?"
Alpha lit up. "That is in the realm of possibility."
"Alpha!" Ally said. "You're supposed to be nice to me."
"Nice does not compute. Truth does," Alpha said.
"Ugh!" Ally changed her clothes and tugged at her new outfit. "You're not really helping me with my nervousness."
"Nervousness is an irrational response!" Alpha snapped.
Ally frowned. "You know what? I think I'll leave you home tonight to charge up."
Before Alpha could reply, Mateo knocked on the door.
"Are you ready to head to the park, Ally?" he called. "Julius and Bethany are meeting us there with some picnic food."
"Yes," Ally called back. "I'll be ready as soon as I power down Alpha. She's acting glitchy again!"
On the way to the park, Mateo's phone pinged. He had a text from Barry: I spent three hours developing the recipe for the hand pies. They turned out fantastic!
"That's great," Ally said.
"It is!" Mateo said as he scrolled down. "Or maybe not. Look at this."
But then Jerry told me that the Food Dude announced they're serving chocolate-filled hand pies!

"Ugh," Ally groaned. "That's the second time another team came up with a dish that's just like ours." She halted and looked at Mateo. "Is it me, or does that seem really strange? It can't be just a coincidence, can it?"
"I was thinking the same thing," Mateo said with a frown. "Something fishy is going on around here."
"And chocolaty!" Ally said.
"I think there's a mole," Mateo said.
"What do moles have to do with this?" Ally asked. "Don't they live underground?"
"Not that kind of a mole," Mateo said. "I mean a mole, like a spy. Maybe someone is feeding information to the other teams."
Ally gasped. "I can't believe anyone would do that!"
"Me neither, but it's the only explanation," Mateo said.
Ally nodded. "We've got to figure out who it is, or we'll lose the contest before it even begins. But how do you catch a spy? We don't have them on Astralia."
"I guess it's hard to keep secrets when everyone can read minds," Mateo said.
"That's it!" Ally cried. "I'll read everyone's minds to find out who's spying on us!"
"Everyone?" Mateo gestured to the people who were pouring into the park to watch the eclipse.
"If that's what it takes," Ally said firmly, "that's what I'll do! And I'm going to start right now. Any one of these people here in Sandville could be the spy!"
Inside the park Ally began scanning people's minds. Mateo kept trying to hurry her along.
"Hmm, people are mostly thinking about the eclipse," Ally said.
"Ally, Mateo!" Julius waved to them from across the green. "Over here!"
Ally and Mateo went over to their friends' blanket.
"Sorry we're late," Mateo said. "We got a text from Barry that made us worried. We think someone is spying on us and sharing our recipes with the other teams."
Bethany looked stunned.
"Whoa! Who are the possible suspects?" Julius asked.
As they ate, Mateo answered Julius' question. "It's got to be someone who spends a lot of time at the diner. I doubt it's Randy or Phil."
"And Flo would never spy on us," Ally said.
"Ooh!" Bethany gasped. "The eclipse is starting."
Ally looked up. The moon was turning a beautiful red color. She felt a chill go up her spine, and goosebumps appeared on her arms.
"It reminds me of Zorgab 8!" Ally cried.
Julius looked at her, confused.
"Never mind! Ha-ha! That's an old joke."
Julius laughed and nodded, but he still looked confused.
"Ugh!" Ally thought. "What is he thinking about me right now? Probably that I'm weird, and he'll never date me again!"
She tried to read Julius' mind, but she couldn't hear any thoughts. Instead all she heard was a buzzing sound, like static. She was about to try again when Julius looked at her.
"I'm glad you're here." He smiled.
Ally smiled back, forgetting to worry about his thoughts. Instead she watched his smile—and the bright red moon above.
After the eclipse the kids started packing up their picnic.
"That was amazing!" Julius said. "It makes me want to learn more about the moon and space stuff."
Mateo grinned. "Ally's a space expert. Hey, Ally. You should take Julius to the UFO museum."
"How about tomorrow?" Julius said.
Ally blushed. "Okay."
"Do you two want to come?" Julius asked Mateo and Bethany.
Mateo shrugged. "We have plans. Right, Bethany?"
"Yep." Bethany nodded.
"Hmm," Ally thought. "Why is Julius inviting them? Maybe he doesn't want to be alone with me."
She tried to read Julius' mind again, but it didn't work.
"That's so strange," Ally thought. "Maybe—" Suddenly something caught her eye. Across the green Flo was talking to a woman.
"Flo!" Ally waved, but Flo just stared at her blankly. Then Flo and the woman fled the park.
"Who was that, Ally?" Julius asked.
"Flo. She works at the diner. I think she's mad at me."
Julius shrugged. "She looked like she didn't want to be seen or something. Maybe she's the mole."
"No way," Mateo said. "Flo and Papi are close."
"I read a lot of spy novels," Julius said. "Spies are trained to get close."
Ally shook her head. "There's no way Flo is the mole—and I'll prove it tomorrow at work."
The next day Ally kept trying to talk to Flo. But the diner was so busy, she finally decided to try reading Flo's mind.
Reading minds had always been easy for Ally. She'd never had to think about what to do. But today was different. Whenever she tried to hear Flo's thoughts, all she heard was static.
"It's like I forgot how to do it." Ally turned, trying to read the thoughts of a few customers.
"Oh no!" She started to panic when she heard the static again. "Something's wrong with me!" Suddenly something occurred to her. "Maybe Alpha is right. Maybe I am becoming too human!"
At the end of the lunch rush, Ally finally got a chance to talk to Flo.
"So . . . " She kept her voice light. "Did you hear another food truck is making chocolate hand pies?"
"No," Flo said.
"It's the second time that another team seemed to steal our idea." She shook her head. "It's almost like someone is giving away our secrets."
"Huh." Flo shrugged and walked away.
"Flo doesn't even seem to care," Ally thought as Barry arrived.
"Hey, Ally." Barry yawned. "I was up all night, but I finally came up with a recipe that no one else will think of. Mateo is going to meet me at the food truck later to test it out. It's—"
Ally slapped her hand over his mouth. "Don't say it out loud!"
"Why not?" Barry mumbled.
Ally glanced around before releasing her hand. "It's not safe!"
"Okay." Barry nodded. "I'll keep this recipe close to my chest."
Ally frowned. "Won't that get messy?"
"Hey, Ally!" Later that day Jerry entered the diner with Sally. "We've been hearing about the cool tricks you do while waitressing. Can we film you doing one?"
"Sure," Ally said.
"It'll take my mind off the mind-reading problem," she thought.

Ally put a few doughnuts on a plate and walked across the diner as Sally filmed her. Halfway across the floor, Ally made herself trip. She felt the plate leave her hand. She saw it fly into the air. But when Ally tried to activate her powers, nothing happened.
Crash! The plate smashed onto the floor.
"Ugh! Sorry!" Ally blushed in embarrassment and ran for a broom. "That's never happened before."
"Don't worry about it," Jerry said. "Do you want to try again?"
"Um, maybe not," Ally said. "I'm not having a very good day."
"No problem," Jerry said. "We can try again another time."
Jerry might not have been upset as he and Sally left, but Ally was. As the last customer left, she cleaned up the mess she'd made.
"I don't understand what's happening to me," Ally murmured. "First I can't read minds, and now I can't levitate dishes."
"What's that?" Julius asked as he entered the diner. "You can't meditate? I can teach you."
"Oh!" Ally was embarrassed that he'd heard her, but at least he'd misunderstood. "Sure, thanks."
"So, are you ready for our date?" Julius asked.
"Date?" Ally repeated.
"Oh gosh, you don't want go to the museum, do you?" Julius looked sad.

"No, I do!" Ally said. "I'm sorry. I've been so distracted all day, trying to figure out who the spy is. But I have an idea!" She put the broom and dustpan away. "What if instead of going to the museum, we go looking for clues to track down the spy?"
Julius grinned. "I love that idea! I've always wanted to gather intel. That's spy talk for getting information. Where should we start?"
Ally was about to answer when Flo came out of the kitchen.
"Ally, do you mind closing again for me?" Flo asked.
"Uh, sure, but is everything okay? You're not sick, are you?" Ally asked.
"I'm fine," Flo said. But she looked distracted as she left the diner.
Ally sighed deeply. "I hate to admit it, Julius. But you could be right about Flo. I think we should follow her."
He grinned. "I'm ready when you are!"

Ally quickly locked up the diner, and then she and Julius ran out to follow Flo. They stayed behind her as she walked briskly through town. Suddenly, at a busy corner, Flo halted. As she waited for the traffic light to change, she looked around.
"Quick, duck behind this mailbox!" Julius said.
They waited until Flo started walking again before continuing to follow her across town. They followed her all the way to—
Ally gasped. "Pepe's! She's going into Pepe's! Why in the world is she going in there?"
She quickly closed her eyes. "I have to read Flo's mind!" she thought. But once again, all she heard was the strange static.
Ally sighed, not wanting to believe Flo was the spy. But the proof was right there.
"I can't believe this," she said to Julius. "Ray will be heartbroken, and so will Mateo. But we can't tell Barry yet. He's so impulsive—he could do something crazy."
Ally and Julius hurried to Rolling Ray's.
"Hey, I thought you were going to the museum today," Mateo said.
"Well, I'm glad you're here," Barry said. "You have got to taste my new dish."
"Not right now." Ally waved him off. "I want to talk to Mateo about something."
"After you taste my chocolate-and-peanut-butter-stuffed waffle." Barry said.
"I'll taste it," Julius said.
"Here you go." Barry handed Julius a waffle on a plate.
Julius took a big bite. "This is delicious! But super messy!" he said as he wiped at the chocolate dripping all over his shirt.
"So that's what you meant when you said you were going to keep this recipe close to your chest, Barry!" Ally said.
"Ha-ha!" Barry laughed loudly. "That's funny, Ally!" Suddenly his smile fell. "I just realized—we can't sell something that's super messy." He sighed. "It's back to the drawing board for me!"
"I'm so sorry, Barry," Ally said, and then she whispered to Mateo, "I need to speak with you alone. Now!"
Ally and Mateo stepped away from the food truck.
"What's going on?" Mateo asked.
"A lot!" Ally whispered. "First of all, my powers aren't working."
"Maybe you're just upset because—"
"Ahh!" Just then someone at the truck yelped.
"That sounds like Barry!" Mateo said.
They rushed back to the truck.

"I know." Ally sighed. "Tina's working on it too."

Then Mateo filled her in on Ray's news. "The CEO definitely wants to expand the diner into a chain of restaurants. Papi promised to give him an answer by the end of the week." He looked sad. "It feels like everyone has a big stuff on their minds lately."
"What do you mean?" Ally asked.

Mateo shrugged. "I'm sad about the changes at the diner. And Coach Cross is having problems too. His brother has been super busy, and he's acting strangely. He barely remembers his own name, and he won't step outdoors, not even to go home to sleep."
"Wait . . ." Ally's mouth fell wide open. "Did you say, he won't leave his shop?"

Mateo nodded, and Ally flashed back to her earlier conversation with Tina. In fourth grade, Ally hadn't listened to the lesson about Jorgandians. But earlier today in the alleyway, she'd hung on Tina's every word.
"That's it!" She leaped to her feet. "I have to call Tina! I know who the Jorgandian is—Eli Cross!"
The next morning Ally and Mateo met Tina near the copy shop.
Tina looked worried. "Are you sure you two want to do this? I can confront the Jorgandian by myself."
Ally took a deep breath. "I want to see it get captured."
"Me too," Mateo said. "But, Tina, what exactly are you going to do to it?"

Tina showed them a device strapped to her hip. "This device emits a beam that extracts a Jorgandian from its human body. Then it traps the life-form so I can transport it to the Astralian Court of Justice."
"But what about the real Eli?" Mateo asked.
"He'll be unharmed and have his body back. The extraction process is very simple and safe."
Ally bit her lip. "Remind me again. What am I supposed to do?"
"Get the Jorgandian to confess everything—its reason for following me to Earth and its plan to evaporate us. The Court of Justice will need this proof in order to press charges."
Tina handed Ally a copy shop bag. "There's a small computer chip in this bag. It will record everything that happens."
Ally gulped. "Here I go!"
Her legs shaking, Ally walked into the copy shop. The shades were down and it was empty.
"Eli?" Ally tried to sound normal. "Are you here?" She heard a rustling sound in the back room. "There was, um, a problem with Ray's menus."

"I knew you'd come back!" Eli's eyes glowed a strange red. "We have some unfinished business, Allyzooba from Astralia!" Eli pulled a round disk from beneath the counter and aimed it at her. "I am Ognor the Jorgandian. Surrender!"
Ally threw her hands up. "Please! Don't evaporate me!"

Ognor cackled. "I will evaporate you, unless you immediately summon Commander Tinakron Beta1P. Capturing her will be a great victory for me and my planet! We will hold her hostage until Astralia surrenders to Jorgandia."
Ally gasped. "That's why you followed her to Earth!"
"Yes!" Ognor placed his finger on the trigger. "Only I lost track of her before I could capture her. Call Commander Tinakron now!"
Ally reached for her phone. "Please, please, please," she thought. "This plan can't fail!"
Suddenly the door flew open and Tina rushed in, her extraction device drawn. "Drop your weapon, Jorgandian!"
But Ognor only laughed. "My weapon is more powerful than your silly device."
"We have a secret weapon that will make you completely powerless!" Tina whistled loudly, and Mateo ran in.
"A . . . a human!" Ognor shrieked.
"That's right," Mateo said. "And you won't harm anyone when an Earthling is present. Get him, Tina!"

Tina pointed her extraction device at Ognor. "It is against our Astralian nature to fight you. However, after your extraction, we will transport you to the Court of Justice. They will decide your fate."

As Tina pulled the trigger, there was a whooshing sound. Then bright light flashed, making Ally close her eyes. When she opened them again, Ognor was gone. But trapped inside the clear chamber of Tina's device was a small, green Jorgandian life-form.
"You got him!" Ally was relieved to see the real Eli standing there, shaking his head.
"What's going on?" he asked. "I feel kind of dizzy."
"Everything is fine," Mateo said. "But you might want to call your brother!"
Outside, the three of them cheered.
"That was like an episode of Cosmic Quest !" Mateo grinned. "And Coach Cross is going to be so happy to have Eli back."
Ally turned to Tina. "You're a hero, Commander Tinakron."
"I couldn't have done it alone," Tina said. "The whole universe is a lot safer now, thanks to you two."
That night Ally lay in bed, unable to sleep. "In a couple of days, Alpha, I'm going to be back in my bed on Astralia."
"And I will once again be housed in advanced technology," Alpha said.
"I'm excited but sad too." Ally sighed. "How do I tell everyone that I'm leaving the planet forever?"
"I suggest telling them that you are going to visit your family," Alpha said. "Say you do not know when, or if, you will return."
"Okay." Ally nodded. "Oh no! What about Julius? He's still on vacation. I won't get to say good-bye."
"Place a video call and assure him your leaving has nothing to do with him."
"Wow!" Ally was surprised. "You just gave me some really good advice, Alpha! You have learned a lot about Earthlings. I'll call Julius now—and tell everyone else in the morning."
Ally was looking around her bedroom one last time when Mateo came in.
"I guess it's time." Ally held back tears. "I'm going home."
"Yep," Mateo said. "Thanks again for giving us Alpha's computer."
"Of course! Alpha has no use for it anymore. Alpha's chip is stored safely on Tina's ship."
Ally picked up her bag as Mateo's phone pinged.
"It's Papi," he said. "Can you stop by the diner on your way to the airport?"
"Do you know why?" Ally asked. "I have to meet Tina. And I've already said good-bye to everyone."
"Maybe he's made his decision about Big City Foods and wants to tell us there," Mateo said.
"I'm sorry I won't be here to help, whatever he decides," Ally replied.
"You've already helped us all so much," Mateo said. "I wish we had a way to stay in touch."
"I'll ask my parents to find a way for us to communicate," Ally said.
"Do you think they can?" Mateo said.
"They'd better!" Ally threw her arms around Mateo. "Thank you for being my friend, and for making this planet feel like home."
Mateo was teary too. "You'll always have a home here."
At the diner Mateo held open the door. Inside it was dark and silent.
Ally was confused. "Why are all the lights . . . ?"
The lights snapped on, and shouts of surprise rang out. "Surprise!" Ray, Phil, Kate, Bethany, Randy, and Flo jumped out from behind the counter.
A large sign read "We'll Miss You, Ally!", and all of her favorite foods were laid out on the counter.
"You did all of this for me?" Ally cried. "Wow!"
"We couldn't let you leave town without a party," Kate said.
Ally's eyes were teary again.
"Sandville won't be the same without you," Ray said. "But before we start this party, I have an announcement."
A hush fell over the room.
"Here it comes," Mateo whispered to Ally. They both crossed their fingers.
"I've turned down Big City Foods' offer," Ray said. "The diner is home to all of us. I don't want to change anything or lose what makes it special."
Everyone cheered. "Hooray!"
Ray grinned. "Now let's eat!"
It was finally time for Ally to leave for the airport. When she picked up her bag again, there wasn't a dry eye in the diner.
"It's bad enough that Tina just took a new job at another museum," Phil moaned. "I can't believe I'm losing my favorite server too—all on the same day."
"Hey! What about me?" Flo teased him.
As everyone laughed, Ally turned and winked at Mateo. Her best friend on Earth smiled back.
The second Commander Tinakron's spaceship docked, Ally raced onto her family's ship.
"Mom, Dad!" she called. "I'm back!"
Ally's parents ran to greet her. They waved their arms in the traditional Astralian greeting.
But Ally threw her arms around them instead. "I've missed you so much!"
"We've missed you so much!" Ally's mother wiped away tears.
"Let us look at you," Ally's father said.
Ally released the hug and twirled around.
"You look well and healthy," her mother said.
"I have so much to tell you!" Ally said.

"We can't wait to hear everything, dear," her mother said. "Luckily, we had some spotty transmission with your Alpha a few times while you were gone. We saw you doing some wonderfully kind and helpful things on Earth."
"And you were using your Astralian abilities!" her father said. "We want to hear all the details. But first, Allyzooba, tell us why you embraced us with your arms."
"It's how humans show they love each other," Ally said.
"I see," Ally's mother said. "It is a lovely ritual."
"Very nice." Her father nodded. "Perhaps you can show all your friends this evening at your party."
"Party?" Ally said.
Her mother beamed. "We thought you might want to have a belated birthday party. You were planning one right before you left, remember? And we know how much you love parties."
Ally was startled. That Allyzooba, the one who'd planned parties and loved shopping and wasn't ready for solo missions, seemed far away now.
"Almost as distant as planet Earth," she thought.
She shook her head and smiled. "Thanks, but no party for me tonight. All I want to do is stay right here, at home."
